nome: Programaria
objetivos: Programaria's mission is to empower girls and women through technology and programming. for a girl, the challenge of programming begins even before she tries to learn. there is a lack of examples to inspire her and a surfeit of prejudices and stereotypes that discourage and reinforce the idea that technology is a male field. it is not a lack of interest or ability, programaria believes that it is necessary to review these cultural narratives that say what women can and cannot do, and to offer tools and opportunities for them to learn. our activities are based on three pillars of action: inspire, debate and learn. besides showing real examples of women and projects in order to inspire women to feel motivated and confident to explore the technology fields and also to demystify the programming universe by showing its opportunities, we encourage the debate about the lack of representation of women in the field, qualifying the discussion about why women are a minority in these areas and the hostile environment they often encounter. finally, we promote opportunities to learn programming in a safe and friendly environment, composed only of women

nome: Gender approach in the National Cybersecurity Policy of Chile
objetivos: 1) The State must start by identifying, through periodic studies and surveys, the main risks, threats and shortcomings suffered by women in Chile in the face of the development and use of cyberspace. For such purposes, they must include the indicators for the development of the gender perspective in cybersecurity, identifying the origin of the shortage of women dedicated to cybersecurity in Chile. 2) The State must prevent the argument of national security from being an excuse for state and municipal authorities to execute disproportionate security measures to the detriment of the fundamental rights of citizens and specifically of women. 3) The State and society in general should direct their efforts to encourage girls and adolescents to study careers related to cybersecurity. 4) Finally, the body in charge of personal data protection must grant efficiency and effectiveness to the new regulations issued on data protection, for which it must consider the gender approach when issuing its reports, guidelines and decisions

detalhes: Iniciativa catalogada no UNESCO Open Science Initiatives (dataset pbs002, ID 299): Women in Data Science (WiDS) Worldwide. Escopo: International. Pilares de igualdade de gênero: Implementing policies and actions that promote inclusion, diversity and equity - to create work environments that attract, retain and advance women scientists; Developing innovative and inspiring educational strategies and initiatives - to open educational pathways for girls in science; Enhancing the visibility of female role models - to dismantle gender stereotypes and biases in science. Descrição: Known as “WiDS”, the Women in Data Science initiative was launched at Stanford University in 2015 with a one-day technical conference featuring outstanding women doing outstanding work in the field. Soon after, volunteer ambassadors took WiDS around the world by organizing similar conferences in their communities under the WiDS umbrella. The WiDS community grew to include additional year-round programming in education, innovation and leadership to strengthen community connections, and support, educate and inspire women everywhere. The annual WiDS programming now includes 200+ conferences and events around the world, a global datathon, a podcast series, a WiDS Academy with upskilling workshops, the Next Gen outreach program, and the UpLink platform for career and training opportunities. WiDS Worldwide programs reach over 150,000 participants each year in more than 160 countries. Since early 2023, WiDS Worldwide has been a fiscally sponsored project under Community Initiatives, with continued strong collaboration and partnership with Stanford. detalhes: Iniciativa catalogada no UNESCO Open Science Initiatives (dataset pbs002, ID 324): The Brilliant Mind (Brilhante Mente) Project. Escopo: Institutional. Pilares de igualdade de gênero: Developing innovative and inspiring educational strategies and initiatives - to open educational pathways for girls in science. Descrição: The Brilliant Mind ( Brilhante Mente ) Project seeks to inspire and empower girls and women to pursue careers in exact sciences, with a special focus on Physics, by applying statistical and computational physics to neuroscience. Through interactive activities, lectures, and workshops, the project aims to create a supportive and inclusive environment, equip participants with the tools to navigate scientific careers and challenge gender stereotypes. With an interdisciplinary approach, the project connects participants with leading scientists, promotes female empowerment in science, and builds a strong support network for future researchers. Key initiatives include mentorship between undergraduate, graduate, and junior scientific initiation students to combat impostor syndrome. Teaching younger students helps undergraduates and graduates recognize their scientific competencies and build confidence. The project offers hands-on research activities in statistical physics and programming, encouraging the replication and publication of scientific studies. Lectures and discussions hosted by the project cover a broad range of topics, including career development, gender, race, class, feminism, ableism, motherhood, mental health, and harassment, advocating for policy solutions and collective action. Additionally, the project seeks to increase the participation of underrepresented groups in academia, such as mothers, people with disabilities, indigenous women, quilombolas, and those in or leaving the socio-educational or prison systems. Throughout 2025, 20 female students from public schools in the state of Alagoas, Brazil, will receive a scholarship to participate in the project's activities. The project received funding from the Brazilian agency under the Call CNPq/MCTI/MMulheres No. 31/2023 – Girls in Exact Sciences, Engineering, and Computing. Pilares de igualdade de gênero: Developing innovative and inspiring educational strategies and initiatives - to open educational pathways for girls in science. Descrição: Since 1998, Ayni Bolivia ( https://redayni.org/tic-mujeres/ ) has been committed to reducing the digital divide in public schools across slum and rural areas, positively impacting over 30,000 underprivileged children and youth. Building on this legacy, the organization launched the Mujeres TIC-Ayni Bolivia programme to address gender inequalities by equipping young women (aged 14–20) with essential digital skills. This initiative promotes awareness of women’s rights, domestic violence prevention, and the dangers of online trafficking while improving technical proficiency in computer maintenance, safe internet use, and entrepreneurship. The programme has achieved great impacts, directly training nearly 2,000 students and over 200 public school teachers during four years, with an indirect reach of 30,000 beneficiaries. Its impact includes increased digital literacy, greater female participation in technological fields, improved parental engagement in education, and enhanced vocational prospects, contributing to family income and self-confidence among participants. In 2025, Ayni Bolivia will expand its efforts by integrating AI and STEM-focused training, further empowering young women to explore technological sectors and develop innovative market opportunities, particularly in underserved areas. Read more about the programme here: https://redayni.org/estudiantes-mujeres-expertas-en-mantenimiento-de-computadoras/ https://redayni.org/2020/05/04/taller-virtual-ciberseguras-2/ www.ayni.nl Contributed by: Sylvia Ortega, Ayni Bolivia, Bolivia Site oficial: https://www.itu.int/net4/wsis/archive/stocktaking/Project/Details?projectId=1514993958

Descrição: Women In Science Without Borders (WISWB) is a gender-inclusive global network of female and male scientists with other stakeholders including policymakers and industry from over 70 countries worldwide. WISWB has worked to establish healthy relations between males and females in scientific communities, taking science as a common template and language for mutual understanding, inclusion, and advocacy for global concerns and marginalized communities as refugees and at-risk scholars. It has empowered scientists as change makers specifically female scientists with leadership skills, providing them with the necessary tools to enhance their actions in their workplaces and societies, which will be useful for the whole scientific community on local and international levels and will increase the impact of science in societies for the sake of global development. WISWB enhances inter-gender, intergenerational, interregional and interdisciplinary scientific collaborations and considers these aspects the keys to a sustainable future. WISWB’s flagship programs include the World Forum Women in Science, launched in 2017, which explores themes within sustainable development goals and other vital topics such as women’s empowerment in STEM fields, innovation, science diplomacy, science communication, leadership and entrepreneurship. Additional WISWB initiatives include the Youth Science Forum, expert-led webinars addressing pressing global challenges, mentoring schemes that celebrate success stories and nurture emerging talent, and the Science Is What the World Needs Forum. Descrição: The “Supporting Women in Science” (SWIS) programme, is a flagship program at the Aga Khan University led by the Institute for Global Health and Development which spans all its campuses in South-central Asia, East Africa and United Kingdom. The program was developed in collaboration with the Center of Global Child Health at SickKids, Canada, and University of Oxford, UK, and offers early- and mid-career female researchers in South-Central Asia and East Africa the opportunity to progress their careers in the field of women's reproductive and perinatal health and other aspects of public health through a phased, competitive, training and research fellowship programme. The SWIS programme utilizes online and distance learning with a self-paced approach with supervision and mentorship. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, through a pre-defined eligibility criterion. Phase I involves online self-learning courses covering a core and elective curriculum over 6 months which is then evaluated formally in Phase II. Eligible candidates then move to Phase III, a mentored fellowship where they develop research proposals and receive funding for research project development, implementation, and evaluation over a 12-month period. The rigorous reporting and monitoring mechanisms track compliance and progress. The online format, offered at no cost, enhances program accessibility, particularly in the post-COVID era. Additionally, SWIS prioritizes mentorship by selecting experienced professionals with strong research backgrounds and mentorship skills to guide participants. The programme evaluation will be based on selected success metrics including program completion ratio, funding opportunities availed by the participants, and validated scholarly output and presentations at key events. Descrição: In 2023, the international non-profit organization Mothers in Science ( https://www.mothersinscience.com/ ) launched a global call to action outlining a set of specific and actionable strategies to promote inclusion of caregivers and close the gender gap in research funding, with multiple good practices collected and shared. It urges research funders worldwide to begin taking meaningful action and use this action plan as guidance to improve their practices and to cultivate a culture of fairness and inclusion more broadly in the STEMM sector. The recommended actions include: (1) Provide financial support to ensure research continuity, (2) Provide flexibility to parents and caregivers, (3) Eliminate bias and discrimination, (4) Simplify grant applications and reform the evaluation process, (5) Measure and monitor diversity and inclusion, and (6) Implement support for COVID-19 impact. Descrição: The Parent in Science (PiS) Movement is an initiative that addresses the intersection of parenthood and scientific careers in Brazil and Latin America. Established to fill a critical gap in data and knowledge, the initiative examines the impact of having children on the academic trajectories of both women and men. The Parent in Science (PiS) Movement presents numerous seminars, lectures, talks and publications throughout Brazil and overseas, raising the discussion about motherhood and career. Notably, it has pioneered research to comprehensively assess how parenthood influences scientists’ careers across different academic stages. The initiative also conducted an extensive survey examining the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the scientific community in Brazil. Its advocacy efforts have led to tangible policy changes, with maternity leave now recognized by funding agencies and research institutions as a factor in curriculum evaluation. Descrição: CARIRITEC is committed to addressing gender bias, increasing female enrolment, and enhancing the retention of girls in courses related to Exact Sciences, Engineering, and Computing. The initiative promotes social inclusion by disseminating knowledge, challenging stereotypes, and promoting the participation of women in STEM fields through a series of targeted activities. At the university level, CARIRITEC organizes laboratory visits where students can observe experiments and practical applications of classroom concepts, sparking their curiosity and encouraging them to pursue studies in STEM disciplines. Lectures featuring women professionals in STEM provide female students with role models, fostering motivation and demonstrating the attainability of their professional aspirations. Additionally, the annual Semiarid Technological Week offers short courses, workshops, and roundtable discussions, enriching the academic experience of female undergraduates. Beyond the university, CARIRITEC delivers lectures in schools to introduce students to representative women in STEM and counteract regional stereotypes. The initiative also leverages digital platforms to facilitate communication and knowledge exchange, with an active presence on Instagram (@cariritec_ufcg) to share updates, news, and insights on women’s participation in STEM. The project has led to a measurable increase in female enrolment in STEM courses at the Semiarid Sustainable Development Centre, with participating students reporting that exposure to inspiring female role models has strengthened their determination to pursue their ambitions. Descrição: The Dedicated App Girls ( Garotas Applicadas ) project, developed by the Associação Efigênia Vidigal de Educação e Cultura (Avec), seeks to promote the participation of girls and women in science and technology by equipping them with the confidence and technical skills necessary to thrive in STEM fields. Targeting high school and ninth-grade students, primarily black and brown girls aged 13 to 17 from public schools, the initiative guides participants in developing mobile applications designed to address real-world challenges they have identified. The programme offers structured instruction in programming, personal development, leadership, business, and entrepreneurship through three-hour sessions held on Saturdays. Additionally, Discussion Circles with Inspiring Women provide mentorship and role models, fostering motivation and self-belief. A distinctive feature of the project is the involvement of psychologists, who lead discussions on critical topics such as affection, internet use among teenagers, self-esteem, and identity, contributing to the holistic development of participants. All activities are offered free of charge and are made possible through the support of partners and volunteers. The project operates as a collaborative effort involving Avec, partner institutions, the local community, and the students themselves, working collectively to foster a more inclusive and diverse STEM landscape. Descrição: Soapbox Science is an international science popularization event that originated in the United Kingdom and has since expanded globally. Launched in Maceió, Brazil, in 2020, the local edition was led by women scientists at the Universidade Federal de Alagoas. Throughout a two-day event, 12 women researchers from diverse fields—including technology, science, medicine, and engineering—engaged directly with the public to present the significance of scientific research and showcase the expertise and contributions of women researchers. Activities should occur in accessible public spaces, including a shopping mall and a beach, promoting dialogue between scientists and non-academic audiences. Due to the pandemic, the activities have happened online. Complementary outreach efforts included a dedicated YouTube channel featuring livestream discussions ( https://www.youtube.com/c/SoapboxScienceMacei%C3%B3/videos ) and an active presence on Instagram ( https://www.instagram.com/soapboxsciencemaceio ). Running until 2023, the initiative was extended to include more women researchers from institutions across Brazil and culminated in the publishing of a book, Soapbox Science Maceió: Dissemination of Science by Women ( Soapbox Science Maceió: Divulgação de Ciência Feita Por Mulheres ) ( https://www.edufal.com.br/ebooks/202481522183498.pdf ). Contributed by: Fernanda Selingardi Matias, Physics Institute, Federal University of Alagoas, Brazil Site oficial: http://soapboxscience.org/soapbox-science-2020-maceio/

Descrição: Mentors in Science ( Mentoras en la Ciencia ) was a capacity-building initiative to address the “leaky pipeline” among Mexican STEM researchers, implemented from 2021 to 2024 by the British Council Mexico in two phases with the support of the UK Government's grant-in-aid. The first phase sought to train female scientists and researchers affiliated with Mexico's prestigious network of researchers (SNII) as mentors and provide them with tools to accompany young female researchers in their professional careers and share good practices that allow them to reach leadership positions and access financial support for their research projects. The second phase consisted of offering guidance to alumni mentors interested in establishing mentoring schemes within their higher education institutions, thereby extending the initiative’s impact, and promoting sustainable mentoring practices in 25 HEIs, including public and private universities, as well as top research centres. This project has impacted more than 1600 women and contributed to enhancing professional competencies, self-confidence, agency, and employability among mentors and mentees. The project succeeded in raising awareness, dismantling gender stereotypes, and identifying gender biases and discrimination. Participants have reported an increase in the publication of research articles and project leadership roles post-project participation. The initiative played a crucial role in fostering networking and cultivating a sense of community and support. Descrição: Co-funded by the ERASMUS+ Programme of the European Union from 2019 to 2022, the W-STEM Project aimed to enhance strategies and mechanisms to attract, admit, and support women in STEM higher education programmes across Latin America. A consortium of 15 universities from Latin America and Europe collaborated to assess gender equality in STEM enrolment and retention rates. Targeting decision-makers and academic staff in higher education institutions, the project focused on developing and implementing institutional policies, strategies, and organizational frameworks to foster greater participation of women at the undergraduate level. Through a series of outreach activities, a mobile app, a mentoring network, and events, W-STEM sought to inspire girls and young women in the final years of secondary education to pursue STEM studies, while providing targeted support during their first year to ensure their retention and support their entry to the STEM workforce. Additionally, the project delivered an online training package to equip higher education institutions with effective tools and practices for promoting gender inclusion and equity in STEM education. detalhes: Iniciativa catalogada no UNESCO Open Science Initiatives (dataset pbs002, ID 266): OWSD-Elsevier Foundation Awards for Early-Career Women Scientists in the Developing World. Escopo: International. Pilares de igualdade de gênero: Enhancing the visibility of female role models - to dismantle gender stereotypes and biases in science. Descrição: Women scientists in developing countries often experience isolation, lack of role models and visibility. Since 2013, the Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) has collaborated with the Elsevier Foundation to address these issues through a unique awards and recognition program for early career women scientists from the global South. This initiative aims to enhance the visibility and career advancement of these scientists, thereby inspiring future generations facing similar challenges. As of 2025, the programme has honoured 65 researchers from more than 35 countries. Each winner receives a cash prize and is sponsored to attend a prominent scientific conference in their field where they receive their awards at a special ceremony, attend workshops and sessions, meet experts, visit local laboratories and institutions, and attend a celebratory networking event. The awards align closely with the United Nations SDGs , welcoming a range of interdisciplinary approaches. The 2023-2026 awards cycle is focused on: 2023: Food Security, agricultural productivity and sustainable food production (SDG2), 2024: Water, sanitation and hygiene (SDG6), 2025: Inclusive Health (SDG3), 2026: Sustainable, affordable and reliable energy (SDG7). Site oficial: https://elsevierfoundation.org/partnerships/diversity-in-stm/womenscientists/

detalhes: Iniciativa catalogada no UNESCO Open Science Initiatives (dataset pbs002, ID 368): Women in Exact Sciences, Engineering and Computing at IM-UFAL. Escopo: Institutional. Pilares de igualdade de gênero: Developing innovative and inspiring educational strategies and initiatives - to open educational pathways for girls in science. Descrição: This initiative aims to inspire and empower elementary and secondary school-aged girls to engage with STEM fields through innovative methods observed in educational research. It places particular emphasis on connecting girls with female role models, drawing on the personal and professional experiences of women in STEM to discuss the challenges that women may encounter in these fields. Coordinated by four professors from Universidade Federal de Alagoas, the initiative also aims to familiarize students with the academic environment of higher education institutions, thereby motivating them to pursue advanced studies. Employing interactive and playful approaches, the initiative features activities such as games, workshops, lectures, panel discussions, visits to campus research laboratories, and complementary classes in exact sciences, computing, and technology. Additional elements include science fairs and competitions in essay and scientific article writing on themes of gender and feminism. The overarching goal is to demonstrate that the ability to produce meaningful work and contribute to a more respectful, equitable, and inclusive world transcends gender. Contributed by: Fernanda Selingardi Matias, Physics Institute, Federal University of Alagoas, Brazil Site oficial: https://femeaufal.wordpress.com/

outrosNomes: Marco Legal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Lei 13.243, de 11 de janeiro de 2016
tipo: Política ou iniciativa de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)
areas: formação e carreira em ciência e tecnologia (STEM)
detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2025 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até setembro de 2026); iniciativa 14098, informada pelo governo do Brasil; última atualização no STIP: 11/08/2025. Iniciativa: Legal Framework on Science, Technology and Innovation - Law 13.243 of January 11, 2016 (Marco Legal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Lei 13.243, de 11 de janeiro de 2016). País: Brasil. Período: desde 2016, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Carreiras de pesquisa). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Supply (MAPA; Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento); Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação); Ministry of Finance (MF; Ministério da Fazenda); Ministry of Health (MS; Ministério da Saúde). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Federal law established to foster the scientific development, research, scientific and technological capacity-building and innovation. Objetivos: 1) Foster scientific and technological activities as strategies for economic and social development. 2) Foster cooperation and interaction among public and private sectors, and companies. 3) Strengthen operational, scientific, technological and administrative capacities of scientific and technological institutions. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Investidores privados; Empreendedores; Instituições de ensino superior; Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Laboratórios privados de P&D; Governo nacional; Governos subnacionais; Empresas de qualquer idade; Empresas de qualquer porte; Incubadoras, aceleradoras e parques tecnológicos; Escritórios de transferência de tecnologia. Temas no STIP: Mudança estrutural no sistema público de pesquisa; Internacionalização da pesquisa pública; Mobilidade intersetorial; Carreiras de pesquisa; Governança internacional de CTI. Instrumentos: Estratégias, agendas e planos (Legal Framework on Science, Technology and Innovation - Law 13.243 of January 11, 2016); orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: Law no. 13.243, 2016 alters Law no. 10.973, 2004 (Innovation Law) and aims to foster cooperation between public research institutions and the private sector. (continuação) The new legislation states that the government must have specific policies concerning the internationalization of PRIs, including aspects such as funding, management and support. Full implementation of the new legislation, however, need further regulation by executive order.

Contexto: CONICET has always been involved in the training of scientists. In the present it finances one third of the doctoral students in the country. Changes in policy are related to regional and disciplinary priorities.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The National Literacy Plan is a public policy coordinated between the national government and the 24 jurisdictions of Argentina, aimed at reversing the reading comprehension deficit and ensuring that all children in the country learn to read and write properly. Objetivos: 1) The primary goal is to ensure that all students in the Argentine Republic can effectively read, comprehend, and produce texts that are appropriate for their educational level. 2) Early Literacy Mastery: Guarantee the development of appropriate reading and writing skills for students by the time they reach 3rd grade. 3) Continuous Support: Provide equitable literacy opportunities to accelerate learning for students from 4th grade onwards. 4) Systematic Tracking: Develop and implement tracking and evaluation mechanisms that allow for continuous improvements in the quality and equity of education. Trecho sobre mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade: "This initiative, which corresponds to an update of the document published in 2015, renews the institutional commitment with this theme and has among its purposes to promote and enhance gender equality in the development of scientific and technological activity; make visible the development of the countrys science and…" | "Promote and enhance gender equality in the development of scientific and technological activities.". Objetivos: 1) It is an instrument designed considering the particularities of the national community of researchers, but also the workers and collaborators who work in CONICYT. País: Colômbia. Período: desde 1996, sem data de término informada. (continuação) Contexto: The process of recognition and measurement of research groups and researchers in Colombia began in 1996, when Colciencias defined research groups as the fundamental unit for generating and applying scientific knowledge. Over the years, the model evolved through multiple adjustments, such as the introduction of the ScientiCol index, differentiated categorizations (A1, A, B, C, D), and the adoption of platforms like GrupLAC and CvLAC for real-time information management. In 2024, the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation updated the process to further promote inclusion and research quality by introducing differentiated evaluation windows for women researchers with children, increasing the weight of social appropriation of knowledge and public science communication outputs, and recognizing open-access publications. This continuous evolution reflects Colombia’s commitment to strengthening its National STI System by improving the visibility, evaluation, and quality of scientific and technological production.

(continuação) Contexto: El Gobierno Federal, a través del CONACYT convoca a la población en general a concursar por una beca para realizar estudios en programas de posgrado de Instituciones de Educación Superior (IES) ubicadas en México y en el extranjero, a realizar actividades académicas, así como para obtener apoyos específicos que atiendan a poblaciones históricamente excluidas, como la población indígena, madres jefas de familia y personas con discapacidad. En 2020 y 2021 se destinó en promedio el 45% del presupuesto del Programa de Becas de Posgrado para promover la igualdad entre mujeres y hombres. Del total de Becas Nacionales Administradas en el periodo 1 de septiembre de 2020 y el 30 de junio de 2021, 47.7% apoyan a mujeres y 52.3% a hombres. Del total de Becas al Extranjero Administradas, 44.6% se asignaron a mujeres, mientras que 55.4% a hombres.

Iniciativa: 5th National Science, Technology and Innovation Conference - Violet Book (5a. Conferência Nacional de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação) [5a. CNCTI]. País: Brasil. Período: de 2025 a 2030. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo; o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão; o texto menciona mulheres ou gênero). Trecho sobre mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade: "Promote equity and diversity in science by including women, Black people, indigenous peoples and other marginalised groups in research policies, implementing racial and gender quotas, creating gender equity committees, and supporting parenting in science.". Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation - Brazil (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Brasil). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The 5th National Science, Technology and Innovation Conference (CNCTI) highlighted the social role of science through free conferences. These events culminated in the creation of the e-book Social Participation in the Preparatory Events of the 5th CNCTI. The Purple Book contains the report of the national stage of the 5th CNCTI and other related initiatives. Objetivos: 1) Promote the solidarity economy and social inclusion by creating integrated public policies focused on cooperatives and production networks, and establish ongoing calls for proposals to support initiatives in this field. 2) Develop assistive technologies by creating a national system for their development and distribution, alongside specific financing programmes for projects in this sector, ensuring accessibility especially in vulnerable regions. 3) Strengthen agroecology and family farming by creating a science, technology and innovation platform focused on agroecology, enhancing research with indigenous and traditional communities, promoting family farming with adapted innovations, and establishing a rural extension network. 4) Promote equity and diversity in science by including women, Black people, indigenous peoples and other marginalised groups in research policies, implementing racial and gender quotas, creating gender equity committees, and supporting parenting in science.

Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation - Brazil (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Brasil). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Lilac Book compiles information and recommendations gathered during the three days of the National Conference. It serves as the foundation for developing the new national strategy for Science, Technology and Innovation (ST&I) covering the period up to 2030, along with an action plan addressing societal challenges to foster a fair, sustainable, and developed Brazil. Objetivos: 1) Reinforce the alignment of science, technology and innovation policies with social demands to promote sustainable and inclusive development in Brazil. 2) Stimulate the emergence of programmes that contribute to reducing social inequalities, tackling climate change, and promoting equitable access to knowledge. 3) Promote policies and programmes for communicating science to society, emphasising popularising science and strengthening scientific education. 4) Expand programmes for Technological Diffusion, Social Technologies, and Creative and Solidarity Economy to foster inclusion and social development. 5) Increase the participation of underrepresented groups in science, technology, and innovation to ensure greater diversity and inclusion. 6) Incentivise programmes integrating ancestral technologies with modern science to generate creative, sustainable solutions that value traditional knowledge. Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The National Programme for Science Popularisation (POPCiencia) aims to develop scientific culture and stimulate the practice of science, technology and innovation. It focuses on promoting social inclusion and reducing social inequalities through these efforts. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation - Brazil (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Brasil). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): This programme aims to expand the use of digital technologies and scientific experimentation within basic education. It focuses on integrating STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics) approaches to enhance teaching and learning. The initiative supports the pedagogical use of digital tools and fosters collaboration between schools, higher education institutions, and civil society. Objetivos: 1) Provide opportunities for the development of skills and abilities related to knowledge in science and technology, with a STEAM approach (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics). 2) Promote productive inclusion and the development of local arrangements. 3) Promote innovation and quality in teaching and learning of science and digital and media education. 4) Encourage the pedagogical use of digital technologies in basic education schools. 5) Encourage the use of active teaching methodologies. 6) Promote digital literacy, teaching and learning through research and scientific experimentation aimed at problem-solving and project guidance. Público-alvo: Professores; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Competências STEM; Cultura de ciência, tecnologia e inovação. Instrumentos: Campanhas de conscientização e divulgação; avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The programme is led by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation in Brazil. It seeks to intensify the qualification of basic education teachers in scientific, digital and media education and to foster communities of practice among basic and higher education teachers to reduce the research-practice gap.

Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation (MinCiencia; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The National Data Centers Plan (PDATA) is a cross-sectoral policy initiative led by the Government of Chile that aims to position the country as a Latin American hub for sustainable digital infrastructure. It promotes investment in the data centre industry while ensuring environmental responsibility, territorial equity, and technological development in areas such as artificial intelligence and renewable energy. The Plan includes regulatory simplification, public-private coordination, and strategic investments in infrastructure, talent, and digital capacity. Objetivos: 1) Encourage the growth of the Data Center industry through investment support by clarifying regulations and organising relevant information to provide certainty to investors and make Chile an attractive destination for digital infrastructure investment while maintaining high environmental standards. 2) Build a decentralised Data Center industry with low environmental impact, powered by renewable energy, reducing energy and water consumption, enhancing resilience to climate challenges, and promoting balanced economic growth benefiting all regions equitably. 3) Strengthen research and development (R&D) to support the growth of data technologies by promoting R&D, training specialised workers, introducing new technologies, and enhancing collaboration between the public sector, academia, and industry to support the digital economy and benefit the population. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira; Doutorandos; Instituições de ensino superior; Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Governo nacional; Governos subnacionais; Empresas de qualquer porte; Associações empresariais.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The reindustrialisation policy aims to increase the generation of added value in the production of goods and services across economic sectors through a cross-cutting commitment to territories and their productive fabric, alongside intersectoral strategic initiatives at the national level. Objetivos: 1) Strengthen the capabilities of human talent, the use and adoption of technologies, access to capital and financing, and physical and digital infrastructure to increase efficiency in the production of goods and services and close productivity gaps. 2) Increase the diversification and sophistication of the Colombian productive matrix by strengthening productive vocations and quality standards to reduce dependence on the mining and energy sector and increase domestic and exportable supply. 3) Strengthen the consolidation of productive linkages between sectors and regions of the Colombian economy, as well as its integration into global value chains. 4) Deepen Colombia's integration with Latin America and the Caribbean, Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America to balance its international relations and enhance the use of its FDI flows. 5) Implement improvements to the institutional and incentive framework to increase value added and thus productivity, competitiveness, and innovation. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation - Brazil (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - Brasil). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Biomes of Brazil Program, led by Brazil’s Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI) under the Program for Biodiversity Research (PPBio), focuses on the conservation and sustainable management of the country’s six major biomes: Amazonia, Cerrado, Caatinga, Atlantic Forest, Pantanal, and Pampa. It employs standardised ecological monitoring methods such as the RAPELD methodology and fosters partnerships with Indigenous groups and institutions. The programme maintains open-access biodiversity databases and supports applied research, digitisation of biological collections, and integration of findings into strategies addressing deforestation, climate risks, and bioeconomy development. Objetivos: 1) Advance biodiversity research and monitoring through standardised methodologies (e.g., RAPELD) for cross-biome ecological studies. 2) Strengthen conservation strategies across Brazil’s six biomes to address deforestation and climate impacts. 3) Promote sustainable use of biodiversity by integrating traditional knowledge from Indigenous and local communities with scientific research. 4) Develop open-access databases (e.g., SiBBr) and digitise biological collections to democratise biodiversity data for policymakers and stakeholders. 5) Support capacity building through training programmes for researchers, students, and communities in biodiversity management. 6) Align with national and global policies, including Brazil’s National Biodiversity Policy, Sustainable Development Goals, and the Convention on Biological Diversity. Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Within the framework of the National Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Minciencias) promotes mission-oriented research and innovation policies (PIIOM) as a transformative strategy to address the country's structural challenges and reduce territorial, social and productive gaps. This approach fosters the articulation of scientific, technological and social capabilities through an action research methodology that prioritises collective challenges and the construction of situated knowledge. It guides public investment towards measurable and highly relevant results by connecting knowledge generation with the real needs of territories and their populations. The initiative also integrates policy instruments with a differential approach to generate significant and tailored impacts in line with the social, cultural, environmental and economic realities of each territory. Objetivos: 1) Promote the transformation of the Colombian economy through strengthening value chains oriented to bio-based products and services. 2) Guarantee the dialogue and creation of knowledge, and the development of appropriate technology and research around agroecology implemented by the ACFEC, with social participation including communities from different regions, free of conflicts of interest, contributing to the human right to food and food sovereignty. 3) Ensure the incorporation of new services, business models and national technological developments in renewable energy generation projects, energy efficiency, conversion technologies and final energy uses manufactured in Colombia to promote reindustrialisation and energy transition processes.

Responsável: Ministry of Education (MEN; Ministerio de Educación Nacional). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Vision STEM+ is a continuation of a roadmap initiated in 2019 by the Ministry of National Education (MEN) and Parque Explora. Through the strategy "Supernova, expanded learning," it explored the state of the art of the STEM/STEAM approach, conducted the NovaCamp camp, and launched the MEN Creative Territory laboratory. Objetivos: 1) To gather the progress made so far to initiate broad conversations that validate a national vision. 2) To serve as a conceptual and methodological platform that articulates other policies within the educational innovation ecosystem related to this approach. 3) To align ongoing efforts towards transforming pedagogical practices through active methodologies, curricular flexibility, interdisciplinarity, and the promotion of 21st-century skills. 4) To establish a system of priorities that advances the implementation of the STEM+ approach. Público-alvo: Professores; Governo nacional; Governos subnacionais; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI. Instrumentos: Estratégias, agendas e planos (Visión STEM+); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: Following these experiences, it became evident that Colombia needed a solid conceptual stance to define a national strategy. In 2020, the Organisation of Ibero-American States (OEI) joined the effort to shape this vision. The 2019 work was revisited, references were updated, co-creation sessions and dissemination events were held, and ideas were synthesised. The result is this publication.

Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão; o texto menciona mulheres ou gênero). Trecho sobre mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade: "Promote the development of scientific vocations and 21st century skills associated with the STEAM approach in girls, boys and adolescents using programming, computer science and/or robotics in STEAM learning environments called STEAM Labs.". Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MINCIENCIAS; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Colombia Robotics Program is an initiative by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation aimed at strengthening the STEAM component in education across Colombia. It focuses on creating learning environments equipped with technological tools and training teachers to use these technologies effectively. The programme also facilitates collaboration among actors in the National System of Science, Technology and Innovation (SNCTI) to promote knowledge exchange and social appropriation of scientific knowledge. Currently, it is implementing 29 STEAM laboratories in 13 departments, benefiting thousands of children, adolescents and teachers through pedagogical strategies and technological appropriation. Objetivos: 1) Promote the development of scientific vocations and 21st century skills associated with the STEAM approach in girls, boys and adolescents using programming, computer science and/or robotics in STEAM learning environments called STEAM Labs. 2) Strengthen scientific vocations through the creation of learning environments with technological equipment and the training of teachers in the use of technological tools. 3) Facilitate the articulation of SNCTI actors for knowledge exchange and link professionals with doctorates in a strategy of social appropriation of knowledge. Público-alvo: Professores; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Pesquisa e inovação colaborativas; Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI; Competências STEM; Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI).

Contexto: The Colombia Robotics Program is presented as a comprehensive solution to strengthen Colombia's capabilities in Science, Technology, and Innovation (CTeI) through the implementation of STEAM laboratories in educational institutions. These laboratories serve as convergence centres for the productive sector, academia and community initiatives, enabling the recognition and exchange of diverse knowledge and practices. They also support the incorporation and adaptation of technologies to local needs following international standards. The programme addresses significant gaps in the development of scientific vocations and the training of human capital in STEAM fields, which currently lag behind international standards. For example, only 1.77% of higher education enrolments in Colombia are in mathematics, science and statistics, compared to an OECD average of 6.24%.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Developed through a collective process starting in 2019, the Ministry of Education (MEN) shared a series of guidelines aimed at fostering educational innovation within schools. These guidelines provide a framework to support educational communities in enhancing quality and equity in education by addressing contemporary challenges in global and local education systems. Objetivos: 1) Explain the meaning and relevance of educational innovation, including concepts, processes, and the development of an innovative culture that positively influences daily school life, teachers' professional lives, and students' learning processes, supporting educational communities in solving school development problems. 2) Provide guidelines for promoting educational innovation across five areas: governance and institutional management; curriculum and pedagogical practices; teacher capacity development; pedagogical knowledge management; and networks and alliances forming an educational innovation ecosystem, all with a territorial approach recognising regional and institutional differences. 3) Describe the monitoring, follow-up, and evaluation model led by the Ministry of Education to measure and periodically monitor educational innovation programmes and initiatives in schools, including access to and use of digital technologies in education. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo; o texto menciona mulheres ou gênero). Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MINCIENCIAS; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The roadmap, prepared by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, outlines Colombia's strategic approach to the ethical and sustainable adoption of artificial intelligence. It includes five strategic work environments, focusing on ethics and governance to promote transparency in algorithms, encourage citizen participation in decision-making, and establish ethical principles and regulatory frameworks for AI development and implementation. Objetivos: 1) Ensure that the Colombian population understands and trusts the artificial intelligence applications developed by organisations through the implementation of 100% of applications that guarantee user privacy, are transparent, responsible and fair, promoting a positive perception and informed participation in society and digital government. 2) Increase the participation of women and underrepresented groups in AI by 50% through educational and training programmes, ensuring a diverse and competent workforce in the field. 3) Implement solid ethical frameworks for the implementation of AI applications, so that 100% of data governance in the field of artificial intelligence is governed by ethical and legal principles. 4) Increase the adoption of artificial intelligence in 50% of companies and government sectors, generating trust through demonstration solutions and continuous education, relying on Colombia's digital government initiatives.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): This initiative promotes the use and adoption of technology to strengthen e-commerce among merchants and the business sector in Colombia. It aims to improve the digital skills of Colombian merchants and micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The project supports the adoption of e-commerce solutions that enable these businesses to offer their goods and services through digital channels, enhancing their online marketing tools to increase sales and productivity. Objetivos: 1) Recognise and segment needs within at least 4,312 Colombian companies and/or merchants to build capacity through human resource training and development, increasing the use and adoption of the e-commerce value chain. 2) Offer the Colombian business community and the popular economy a web tool for registration, counselling, and management of learning and digital skills assessment, with the technical capacity to diagnose their knowledge and adoption of technology in e-commerce. 3) Implement a specialised asynchronous and/or synchronous consulting programme that enables beneficiaries to make their product offerings available online, strengthening their capabilities through timely implementation of technological tools. 4) Provide a platform that allows at least 4,312 Colombian merchants and/or MSMEs to create or strengthen an e-commerce solution as their primary online marketing channel. Público-alvo: Empreendedores; Microempresas; Pequenas e médias empresas. Temas no STIP: Estratégias de política de inovação empresarial; Competências STEM; Transformação digital das empresas. Contexto: The National Planning Department (2023–2026) seeks productive transformation, internationalisation, and climate action. One catalyst focuses on promoting micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises through a strategy that encourages technical, financial, and cultural involvement by adopting digital technologies in the productive sectors.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Intelligent Community Centres (CECIs) form a national network of smart community centres across Costa Rica. Each centre houses a laboratory equipped with state-of-the-art computers, providing various services to local communities. These centres aim to technologically empower communities by facilitating access to knowledge, information, creativity, and the ability to tackle new challenges. The next phase of the initiative plans to offer agricultural, livestock, and industrial extension services to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and to train users in utilising the State's digital administration online services. Objetivos: 1) To promote capacity building in Science and Technology to bridge the existing digital divide in Costa Rica through digital literacy. 2) To contribute to the economic and social development of communities by implementing a programme that enables learning, the use of online services, and the development of skills that promote leadership and entrepreneurship in the local community. 3) To develop a network of centres for public access and use of digital technologies, with national coverage, prioritising communities where the digital and social divides are greatest. 4) To implement a continuous monitoring system for the work carried out in the various community centres, which will identify flaws in the design and implementation plan for their correction. Público-alvo: Grupos desfavorecidos e excluídos; Sociedade civil; Pequenas e médias empresas. Temas no STIP: Apoio não financeiro a P&D e inovação nas empresas; Apoio a PMEs e empresas inovadoras jovens; Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI); Transformação digital das empresas. Objetivos: 1) Promote the coordination and synergy of complementary scientific and technological capabilities across different SNCTI institutions through the execution of research, development, and innovation projects. Drive projects with an interdisciplinary and cross-cutting approach to achieve greater productive, social, and/or environmental impact, regional development, and the design or application of public policies. Optimize the utilization of resources. Foster the "federalization" of the SNCTI, aiming for the strengthening and equitable distribution of the system's capabilities across the national territory. Develop pilot experiences for inter-institutional integration directed toward the consolidation of potential Inter-institutional Centers (CITEs). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Initiated in 2022 under the name "Federal High-Impact Networks Program," this initiative seeks to promote strategic science with impact by strengthening the National System of Science, Technology, and Innovation (SNCTI). The program funds research networks that integrate local and international groups of excellence with emerging teams to address national development priorities. With a federal focus aimed at reducing territorial and institutional asymmetries, it drives large-scale interdisciplinary projects. Its ultimate goal is to ensure the sector's sustainability through human resource training and the transfer of knowledge into tangible, long-term solutions. Objetivos: 1) Promote high-quality research networks focused on strategic areas for national development. 2) Federal High-Impact Networks: Strategic R&D alliances of research groups within the National STI System, characterized by high-level international engagement and the inclusion of young or early-career researchers. 3) By applying federalization criteria based on researcher density and budget execution, the program aims to reduce regional asymmetries by fostering knowledge transfer and strengthening scientific excellence in relatively less developed zones. Responsável: Secretariat of Innovation, Science and Technology (SICyT; Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): This programme provides targeted training in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the public administration, combining practical skills with foundational knowledge, including core cybersecurity concepts. It aims to familiarise participants with key AI concepts, effective prompting techniques, good practices, and selected use cases that illustrate the adoption and application of AI in government settings. The programme is delivered through a blended format—combining asynchronous learning modules with in-person sessions—and concludes with an integrated final component designed to consolidate learning and support its application in the public sector context. Objetivos: 1) To establish a common baseline of knowledge. 2) To foster innovation within the public administration. 3) To lay the groundwork for its future expansion to other government entities. Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Chilean Artificial Intelligence Policy 2021-2030 covers three pillars: (1) enabling factors, (2) development and adoption of AI (3) ethics, regulatory aspects and socio-economic impacts. Objetivos: 1) Insert Chile in the vanguard and global collaboration related to AI, with an ecosystem of research, development and innovation in AI that creates new capabilities in the productive, academic and state sectors, oriented according to cross-cutting principles of opportunity and responsibility, contribute to sustainable development and improve our quality of life. 2) To develop AI's enabling factors which encompasses development of human capital, technological infrastructure and data availability. 3) To foster the use and development of AI which encompasses research, development, innovation, and entrepeneurship based on AI systems. It also foster adoption both in the private and the public sector. 4) To discuss and reach consensus about ethics, standards, cybersecurity and regulation between the private and public sectors for a human-centered development and use of AI. This includes topics such as privacy, transparency, responsibility, environmental issues, gender-gap, automation impacts, among others. Iniciativa: Chile Scholarships (BECAS CHILE). País: Chile. Período: desde 2008, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Pesquisadores de doutorado e pós-doutorado, Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: National Research and Development Agency (ANID; Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): This initiative is an international scholarship programme aimed to support human capital formation abroad. Objetivos: 1) The general objective of this initiative is to improve the quality of the human capital in Chile, by defining a comprehensive long term policy of advanced human capital formation abroad. The programme has three lines of action that correspond to 3 specific objectives of this initiative:. 2) Increase opportunities for basic and advanced training abroad. 3) Streamline and coordinate the government grant programmes. 4) Encourage international cooperation. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Doutorandos. Temas no STIP: Pesquisadores de doutorado e pós-doutorado; Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos. Instrumentos: Bolsas de estudo, de pesquisa e de pós-graduação; orçamento anual informado: de 50 a 100 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Education and innovation are strategic pillars of the action plan of the government of Chile. Becas Chile operates in this context. The programme was initiated in October 2008, before the program was called international scholarships. This initiative responds to the urgent need to have more academic, professional and technical excellence, not only more productive but also more creative, innovative and entrepreneurial. Under the proposal submitted by the Presidential Commission, the innovation strategy for this initiative will be drawn for the next four years. This will be delivered during 2016.

It also promotes scientific research fostering a passion for science and technology; and promoting scientific and technological skills and abilities, both in teachers and in regular basic education students. Education in science and technology is important for the development of the country, to obtain appropriate answers and practical solutions to the problems of our environment. Students from the initial, primary and secondary levels of public and private educational institutions participate at the national level. Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Millennium Science Initiative (ICM) aims to promote the development of cutting edge scientific and technological research in the country, as a key factor for sustainable, long-term economic and social development. Objetivos: 1) Contribute to the increase in Chile’s competitiveness, by improving the quantity and quality of cutting edge S&T research in the country and encouraging researchers to work in synergic groups in order to confront new problems and generate new knowledge. 2) Stimulates and supports the collaborative work of scientific groups through the creation of Centers of Research - "Millennium Institutes" and "Nuclei" - which carry out scientific research that can be compared to that done in more developed countries, in both the natural and exact sciences as well as the social sciences. 3) Contribute to an increase in knowledge in different disciplines, in order to provide solutions for the various challenges that the country faces. 4) Reduce the “brain drain”, as well as attracting excellent Chilean and foreign scientists currently working in other countries to the national system of scientific-technological research. Público-alvo: Instituições de ensino superior; Laboratórios privados de P&D. Temas no STIP: Financiamento competitivo da pesquisa; Carreiras de pesquisa; Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos; Cultura de ciência, tecnologia e inovação. Instrumentos: Financiamento de centros de excelência (Millennium Nucleus Centers); Financiamento de centros de excelência (Millennium Institutes); orçamento anual informado: de 5 a 20 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada.

(continuação) Contexto: The Chilean ICM Programme is implemented in the framework of the international Millennium Science Initiative, a project of the World Bank and the Science Initiative Group to build capacity in science and technology in the developing world. Work to prepare a project to implement the Millennium Science Initiative in Chile started in 1988. In January 1999 a decision was made to deliver to the Ministry of Planning (Mideplan) the responsibility of implementing this Program, adding up to the efforts made on this matter by the Ministries of Education, Economics, Agriculture, Mining and other public and private organizations. As from 1 January 2011, the Millennium Science Initiative program ceases to be a part of the Ministry of Planning and it is transferred to the Ministry of Economics, Development and Tourism. The transfer is mainly based on the fact that given the new institutional structure related to science, technology and innovation development, it is that Minister the one responsible for directing and coordinating the Science, Technology and Innovation National System and its components.

Iniciativa: Science Promotion in Developing Countries [TWAS]. País: Brasil. Período: desde 1983, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Pesquisadores de doutorado e pós-doutorado, Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): TWAS was founded by a distinguished group of scientists from the developing world. Objetivos: 1) To promote scientific excellence and possibilities for scientific development in Southern countries through South-South postgraduate and postdoctoral scholarship programs. 2) To promote mobility of researchers. 3) To support the “ grants ” research. 4) To support recognition of scientists. Público-alvo: Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira. Temas no STIP: Pesquisadores de doutorado e pós-doutorado; Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos; Pesquisa e inovação para países em desenvolvimento. Instrumentos: Financiamento de projetos de pesquisa pública; Bolsas de estudo, de pesquisa e de pós-graduação (TWAS); orçamento anual informado: menos de 1 milhão (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The group of scientists that founded TWAS shared a belief that developing nations, by building strength in science and engineering, could build the knowledge and skill to address such challenges as hunger, disease and poverty. From the start, the Academy had essential support from Italian scientists and political leaders. Since 2004, the National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq - Brazil) and TWAS have launched Calls, annually, which provide for the offer of doctoral and postdoctoral scholarships in Brazil, in the field of natural sciences, to developing countries. There were more than 350 foreign beneficiaries, who were able to develop their research in Brazilian universities. The nationalities of the researchers include countries such as Pakistan, Cuba, Benin, Cameroon, Egypt, Nigeria and Kenya. MCTI voluntarily contributes to the TWAS.

Responsável: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG; Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería); Ministry of Environment and Energy (MINAE; Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía); Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT; Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación, Tecnología y Telecomunicaciones); Ministry of Economy, Industry and Commerce (MEIC; Ministerio de Economía, Industria y Comercio). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The strategy is oriented towards an economy with fossil decarbonization, competitiveness, sustainability and inclusion, through a convergence and coherence between productive development and environmental policies. Objetivos: 1) Making Costa Rica a model country in sustainable development, taking advantage of its biological resources to promote social inclusion and equity, balanced territorial development, conservation, knowledge and sustainable use of its biodiversity, and national competitiveness. 2) Making the bioeconomy one of the pillars of the productive transformation of Costa Rica, promoting innovation, value addition, diversification and sophistication of its economy, applying the principles of circular bioeconomy and seeking fossil decarbonization of production and consumption processes. 3) Promoting convergence between the countrys wealth in biological resources and the use of national capacities in biological sciences for the valorization of that wealth. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo). Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation (MinCiencia; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Digital platform gathering Chile's science, technology, knowledge, and innovation (STKI) data and indicators characterizing its capacities and production on these matters. Objetivos: 1) To support evidence based decision and policy making, as well as to inform the citizenry and relevant Chile’s STKI system stakeholders. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Doutorandos; Professores; Mulheres; Sociedade civil; Instituições de ensino superior; Laboratórios privados de P&D; Governos subnacionais; Empresas de qualquer porte; Escritórios de transferência de tecnologia; Sociedades científicas e academias. Temas no STIP: Inteligência estratégica de políticas; Acesso aberto a publicações; Acesso ampliado a dados e software. Instrumentos: Serviços de informação e acesso a dados; Criação ou reforma de órgão público ou estrutura de governança; orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The need of creating a platform gathering all the data and information of the Chilean STKI system arose from the Law 21105, which created the Ministry of Science. In its article 5, letter i, points out that the Ministry must maintain and manage, in a coordinated manner with other public bodies, information regarding the capacities and production of the country in science, technology and science-based innovation. In the same way, it must maintain and manage statistics and information of public interest regarding the resources that the organisms of the State administration deliver to the public and private sectors in these matters. (continuação) Following that mandate, Observa seeks to deliver reliable technical information in a clear, open and transparent way, reaching both the citizens and STKI system stakeholders, and thus provide evidence and analysis that allows to support public policy decision-making.

Trecho sobre mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade: "Its objective is to promote interest in research among boys, girls, and adolescents, as well as to develop attitudes and skills that enable them to actively participate in a culture of Science, Technology and Innovation (STI)." | "Within the framework of the National Development Plan (PND 2022 - 2026) "Colombia, a World Power of Life," the Ondas program directs its work in conflict, transition, and/or consolidation territories with science, technology, and innovation programs or projects that address social, productive, and/or environmental…". Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MINCIENCIAS; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Ondas Program of the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation is the main strategy for fostering scientific vocations among children and youth. Its objective is to promote interest in research among boys, girls, and adolescents, as well as to develop attitudes and skills that enable them to actively participate in a culture of Science, Technology and Innovation (STI). The program also recognizes children and adolescents as key differential actors for change under the chapter “A Generation Grows for Life and Peace: Children and Adolescents Protected, Loved, and with Opportunities,” promoting their comprehensive development and prioritizing those living in poverty or at risk. Aligned with the national commitment to reducing regional disparities, the Ondas Program implements clear actions with a differential, ethnic, and territorial approach, encouraging the identification of problems faced by children and adolescents, while building local capacities around Bioeconomy and Territory, Energy Transition, and Environmental Protection.

Objetivos: 1) Promote the development of skills and attitudes in science, technology and innovation in children and adolescents in preschool, basic and secondary education. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira; Doutorandos; Professores; Instituições de ensino superior; Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Sociedades científicas e academias; Estudantes do ensino médio. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MINCIENCIAS; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): One of the most significant contemporary challenges is to learn, exchange and build knowledge based on science, technology and innovation (CTeI), so that social groups can use said knowledge to improve our quality of life. Therefore, it is essential to promote and generate processes of Social Appropriation of Knowledge. From the Ministry and within the framework of the Public Policy of Social Appropriation of Knowledge, we understand that the Social Appropriation of Knowledge is a deliberate process that involves all social actors: the scientific community, civil society, the business sector and the State. This process seeks to promote practices of exchange, dialogue, analysis, reaction and negotiation through the management, production and application of science, technology and innovation in environments of trust, equity and inclusion. The objective is that more and more citizens are capable of managing, communicating, generating and appropriating CTeI in different areas of life and in their respective territories.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Departmental Councils for Science, Technology and Innovation (CODECTI) are the highest instance of governance and articulation of policy, strategies, advice and guidance in the Science, Technology and Innovation (CTel) sector, with the actors who develop activities aimed at strengthening scientific, technological development and innovation capacity at the departmental level and the capital district. Objetivos: 1) The purpose of the Decree is to "Regulate the organization and operation of the Departmental Councils of Science, Technology and Innovation, hereinafter CODECTI, as the actors that develop activities aimed at strengthening scientific, technological development and innovation capacity, in the respective departmental scope and in the capital district. The main objective of the Departmental Councils of Science, Technology and Innovation (CODECTI) is to strengthen territorial governance in matters of science, technology and innovation (CTeI), articulating key actors - State, academia, business and civil society - to formulate, advise and coordinate policies, plans and projects that promote regional development. In line with the National Public Policy of CTeI, the CODECTI seek to increase the contribution of the CTeI to the social, economic, environmental and sustainable development of the country, promoting a knowledge society through differential, territorial and participatory approaches. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Competências STEM). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Costa Rican Institute of Technology (TEC; Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica); Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT; Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación, Tecnología y Telecomunicaciones); Ministry of Public Education (MEP; Ministerio de Educación Pública); University of Costa Rica (UCR; Universidad de Costa Rica); Distance State University (UNED; Universidad Estatal a Distancia); National University of Costa Rica (UNA; Universidad Nacional de Costa Rica); National Technical University (UTN; Universidad Técnica Nacional). Objetivos: 1) The main its main objective of the Costa Rican Math Olympiad is to promote students' interest in Math through a process of planning, organization and execution of Olcoma and the selection of young people to represent our country in international events. Contexto: The Costa Rican Mathematics Olympiad is implemented by an executive decree since 1994 and aims to promote students' interest in Mathematics. There is an interinstitutional committee that supervises and develops the process of these Olympiads. It is aimed at students from 7th grade til 12 grades.

Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT; Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación, Tecnología y Telecomunicaciones). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The EU-CELAC Working Group on Research Infrastructures (WG RI). Objetivos: 1) To support policy coordination and the exchange of information to mobilise and strengthen RI cooperation between both regions, contributing to solve the global challenges while facilitating researchers’ mobility and the international access of RI. Público-alvo: Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Laboratórios privados de P&D; Governo nacional; Entidades internacionais. Temas no STIP: Infraestruturas de pesquisa e tecnologia; Internacionalização da pesquisa pública; Financiamento de terceiros; Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos; Governança internacional de CTI; Políticas de inovação orientadas por missões. Instrumentos: Órgãos de coordenação de CTI (International Working Group); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The EU-CELAC Working Group on Research Infrastructures (WG RI) was officially created in March 2017, highlighting the importance of Research Infrastructures (RI) as one of three strategic pillars of the EU-CELAC Common Research Area (CRA). The mandate is clear: “to support policy coordination and the exchange of information to mobilise and strengthen RI cooperation between both regions, contributing to solve the global challenges while facilitating researchers’ mobility and the international access of RI”. Co-chaired by the European Commission and Uruguay Composed by representatives of the EU and LAC Ministers EU Member States represented by national delegates: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, United Kingdom. (continuação) In Latin America and the Caribbean currently 19 countries are members of the Working Group: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Paraguay, Panama, Peru, Dominican Republic, Uruguay and Venezuela Meets at least once a year to decide future steps.
