Iniciativa: Costa Rican Physics Olympiad (Olimpiadas Costarricenses de Física) [Olcofi]. País: Costa Rica. Período: desde 1996, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Competências STEM). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT; Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación, Tecnología y Telecomunicaciones); National University of Costa Rica (UNA; Universidad Nacional de Costa Rica). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Costa Rican Physics Olympiad is an academic competition for students in the field of physics whose main objective is to develop the necessary vocations for the training of comprehensive scientists. The competition is aimed at tenth and eleventh grade students with an interest in the physics. These Olympiad categories are divided into BB for tenth grade students and AA for eleventh grade students which compete in into two stages. Objetivos: 1) To develop scientific knowledge, particularly that of Physics, in secondary school youth throughhigh-quality academic tests. 2) Contribute to the scientific and pedagogical development of High school Physics teachers. Público-alvo: Professores; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Competências STEM; Cultura de ciência, tecnologia e inovação. Instrumentos: Campanhas de conscientização e divulgação; orçamento anual informado: menos de 1 milhão (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The Costa Rican Physics Olympiad (OLCOFI) promotes the generation of more scientific development of Physics, through an active participation of students at the national and international level, both from private and public education schools, where the level of the Olympiads exams reflects the development of creative talent and logical-mathematical intelligence. In addition, an organizing committee perform a vital function for the consolidation of a more equitable competition and with more scientific culture.

Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Guidelines to government actions. Objetivos: 1) To promote ethical principles for responsible development and use of artifical intelligence. 2) To promote investment in artificial intelligence R&D. 3) To remove barriers to innovation in artificial intelligence. 4) To qualify professional to the AI ecosystem. 5) To promote Brazilian AI innovation and development internationally. 6) To foster collaboration among public and private institutions, research institutions and industry in the development of AI. Contexto: The Brazilian AI Strategy was adopted after a series of public consultations and is an important step in the full implementation of the Digital Transformation Strategy. Its actions and indicators still have to be detailed.

Iniciativa: Scholarships for Indigenous People (Fortalecimiento Académico para Indígenas) [FAI]. País: México. Período: desde 2024, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão). Responsável: Secretariat of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation (SECIHTI; Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): In accordance with the National Development Plan, Conahcyt implements actions to provide support to students from indigenous communities who wish to undertake or are already undertaking postgraduate studies. Objetivos: 1) Specifically aimed at students from indigenous populations for postgraduate studies. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Doutorandos; Grupos desfavorecidos e excluídos. Temas no STIP: Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). Instrumentos: Bolsas de estudo, de pesquisa e de pós-graduação; orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: In accordance with the National Development Plan 2019-2024, affirmative actions are implemented to provide support focused on historically excluded population groups. Between 1 September 2020 and 30 June 2021, a total of 3,571 scholarships were administered to support specific populations to promote social inclusion, of which 22.7% (812) went to students from indigenous populations to pursue postgraduate studies, 77.1% (2,754) to Mexican mothers who are heads of household to pursue full-time, school-based professional studies, and 0.2% (5) to incorporate students with disabilities to pursue postgraduate studies.

Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The National Science, Technology and Innovation Policy is a strategic management document that guides the science, technology and innovation actions and activities of SINACTI stakeholders over a time horizon. Objetivos: 1) Strengthen the institutional framework at the strategic levels, implementation and execution of SINACTI. 2) Increase the social appropriation of STI in society at large. 3) Increasing the high-level human capital of SINACTI stakeholders of SINACTI. 4) Improve SINACTI's generation of scientific and technological knowledge, according to the country's priorities. 5) Increase innovation at SINACTI. 6) Improve financial conditions for an environment of STI development, for the benefit of all SINACTI actors. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira; Doutorandos; Professores; Sociedade civil; Instituições de ensino superior; Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Governo nacional; Governos subnacionais; Empresas de qualquer porte; Gestores de programas e equipe de apoio científico. Instrumentos: Estratégias, agendas e planos; orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. tipo: Política ou iniciativa de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)
areas: formação e carreira em ciência e tecnologia (STEM)
detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2025 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até setembro de 2026); iniciativa 99996348, informada pelo governo do Brasil; última atualização no STIP: 11/08/2025. Iniciativa: New Curriculum to Form Engineers Capable of Innovating and to Managing Innovation (Novo curriculo para formar engenheiros capazes de inovater and gerir innovacao: Insper and Isitec.). País: Brasil. Período: desde 2013, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Both are ongoing programs, both in São Paulo. Both are non for profit, non governmental institutions. INSPER is an institute certified by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business - AASCP. ISITEC is an institute created by the Union of Engineers of São Paulo, consisting of a Faculty of Engineering of Innovation. Objetivos: 1) Form engineers inclined to innovate and to undertake business. 2) Form engineers who learn how to learn and to adapt their actions to fast changing technologies. 3) Form engineers able to start their own innovative business. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Instituições de ensino superior; Laboratórios privados de P&D. Temas no STIP: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI. Instrumentos: Extensão tecnológica e consultoria a empresas; avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Both derive from the perception that traditional curriculum in different areas of engineering are outdated, too broad and not specialized enough to form engineers trained to learn new skills permanently and, more important: to innovate and manage innovation and to be entrepreneurs themselves. The new courses and innovative curriculum have been examined and approved by the Ministry of Education.

(continuação) Contexto: In accordance with the Law 9971, law of Creation of the Costa Rican Promoter of Research and Innovation: The National Science, Technology and Innovation Plan is the planning instrument for scientific, technological and innovation development proposed by the Government of the Republic which in its administration period shall have a short, medium, and long- term perspective to give it continuity and outreach to the public, private and education system’s efforts in this matter (Art.16). PNCTI responds to the guidelines outlined in the National Policy for Knowledge-based Society and Economy 2022-2050 (PNSEBC), specifically those destined to development of the CTI. Its three strategic areas shall have three cross-cutting themes and two emerging themes, permeating the plan’s actions. These themes are respectively, the following: Cross-cutting themes: Bioeconomy, Digital technologies, Human Health Research and Life Sciences Emerging Themes: Artificial Intelligence and, Aerospace development.

Iniciativa: Allocation for Science, Technology and Innovation of the General Royalties System (Asignación para la Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación del Sistema General de Regalías (SGR)) [ASCTI - SGR]. País: Colômbia. Período: desde 2012, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão). Responsável: National Planning Department (DNP; Departamento Nacional de Planeación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Allocation of the General Royalties System (SGR) consists of the implementation of public, open and competitive calls, in which any actor of the National STI System can present and execute projects that seek to increase the scientific, technological, innovation and competitiveness capacity of the regions. Objetivos: 1) Increase the scientific, technological, innovation and competitiveness capacity of the regions through projects that contribute to the production, use, integration and appropriation of knowledge in the economy and society in general. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira; Doutorandos; Professores; Sociedade civil; Instituições de ensino superior; Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Laboratórios privados de P&D; Empresas de qualquer porte; Incubadoras, aceleradoras e parques tecnológicos; Sociedades científicas e academias. Temas no STIP: Financiamento competitivo da pesquisa; Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). Instrumentos: Financiamento de projetos de pesquisa pública; orçamento anual informado: de 100 a 500 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Royalties are the economic consideration received by the country for the exploitation of a non-renewable natural resource, such as oil and gas. In 2011, the SGR was created to distribute resources taking into account a greater impact on the entire population. For the year 2019 a reform to the SGR was promoted, which created a new distribution of resources. Of these resources, 10% is destined for STI, benefiting all departments.

Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Graphene Innovation Program, called InovaGraphene-MCTI is one of the strategic and structuring programs of the Brazilian Nanotechnology Initiative (IBN), and is a national vector for the development of graphene and the next generation of carbon-based 2D materials, on the frontiers of physics, chemistry and engineering, in order to create, integrate and strengthen governmental actions in the area, focusing on economic dynamism and market specialization, by promoting innovation in Brazilian industry, to ensure technological autonomy in high technology sectors. Objetivos: 1) Structure the governance and coordinate the efforts of the State. 2) Promote the advancement and strengthening of scientific, technological, innovation and national entrepreneurship. 3) Stimulate the development and reciprocal transfer of knowledge, new technologies and business models between academia and the public and private sectors. 4) Mobilize, articulate and foster national public and private actors to act in a coordinated manner in the development of the graphene area. 5) Ensure universal access to advanced scientific and technological infrastructure in the graphene area. 6) Promote and stimulate the attraction, training, capacity building, mobility and establishment of human capital capable to act in technological development, entrepreneurship and innovation. Público-alvo: Institutos públicos de pesquisa; Laboratórios privados de P&D; Empresas de qualquer porte; Escritórios de transferência de tecnologia; Associações empresariais.

Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo). Responsável: National Council for Humanities, Science and Technology (CONAHCYT; Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Law guarantees the human right to science, strengthens the National Council of Humanities, Sciences and Technologies (Conacyt) as the National Council of Humanities, Sciences and Technologies (Conahcyt), does not restrict freedom of research and promotes increased public funding of progressive way and without regressions; supports the plurality, existence and respect of our ancient cultures and makes knowledge a common good. Objetivos: 1) To guarantee the exercise of the human right to science in accordance with the principles of universality, interdependence, indivisibility and progressivity. 2) Establish the purposes, principles and bases of public policies in the field of humanities, sciences, technologies and innovation, as well as the criteria and means for their formulation, execution and evaluation. 3) Establish the public mechanisms and instruments for the necessary resources and stimuli in order to promote and support training, research, dissemination and development of projects in the field of humanity, science, technology and innovation, as well as open access to information derived from said activities. 4) Establish the attributions of the National Council of Humanities, Sciences and Technologies, as the coordinating body of the National System of Humanities, Sciences, Technologies and Innovation, as well as in charge of formulating and conducting the national policy in matters of humanities, sciences, technologies and innovation. 5) Establish the recognition, coordination, articulation and operation of the Public Centers for Humanistic and Scientific Research, Technological Development and Innovation.

Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): PPBio is a strategic programme at the national level to expand knowledge about the immense Brazilian biodiversity, filling knowledge gaps, especially in regions with difficult access and, therefore, with historical deficits in terms of scientific knowledge. Objetivos: 1) 1) efficiently apply already tested methodologies for monitoring biodiversity and ecosystem services. 2) 2) train and integrate local people responsible for monitoring biodiversity to maximize the quality and availability of information for decision-making on the degradation of environmental services associated with biodiversity, with the aim of minimizing environmental degradation, leading to the sustainable use of resources in natural and anthropized environments, such as agrosilvopastoral and urban, and still maximize the economic return and local and regional well-being. 3) 3) generate models and scenarios for the sustainable use of natural resources in the Brazilian territory and for the different biomes. 4) 4) modeling the impacts arising from extreme weather events and their impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem services, such as fire. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Doutorandos; Institutos públicos de pesquisa. Temas no STIP: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI. Instrumentos: Financiamento institucional da pesquisa pública (Public Call); orçamento anual informado: de 1 a 5 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Expand the formation of new research networks to cover all Brazilian biomes.

Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Competências STEM). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação); Ministry of Economy (ME; Ministério da Economia). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Science in School Program (PCE) is a commitment to improving the teaching of science in education. Objetivos: 1) To improve science teaching in basic education schools. 2) To promote teaching through research aimed at solving problems. 3) To better qualify basic education teachers for science teaching. 4) To stimulate the interest of basic education students in scientific careers. 5) To identify young talents. 6) To encourage the implementation of innovative solutions that contribute to improving science teaching and learning. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Instituições de ensino superior; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Competências STEM; Cultura de ciência, tecnologia e inovação. Instrumentos: Estratégias, agendas e planos (Decree); Campanhas de conscientização e divulgação; orçamento anual informado: de 5 a 20 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: In Brazil, the scientific teaching and learning process in basic education barely integrates educational institutions, be they universities, technological institutes or state and municipal basic education networks, as well as other institutions that deal with scientific production and dissemination (museums, fairs, olympics, etc). The Science in School Program was designed to fill this gap. By bringing university researchers closer to state and municipal education networks, the PCE aims to foster the development of methodologies aimed at integrating institutions, the induction of innovation and the interdisciplinary and collective solution of concrete problems of social reality.

Iniciativa: Programme for the Incorporation of Students with Disabilities Into National Postgraduate Courses (Programa para la Incorporación de Estudiantes con Discapacidad a Posgrados Nacionales). País: México. Período: desde 2013, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão). Atenção: esta iniciativa aparece só na edição 2023 do STIP Compass; o governo não a informou de novo em 2025, e ela pode ter sido encerrada ou substituída. Responsável: National Council for Humanities, Science and Technology (CONAHCYT; Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Strengthen the academic skills of people with disabilities through specific scholarships that enable them to enter postgraduate programmes and contribute to reducing the disadvantages caused by marginalisation, educational inequality and discrimination. Objetivos: 1) To contribute to the entry of people with disabilities to master's studies by strengthening their academic skills, promoting equal access to third level studies and training professionals who contribute to local, regional and national development. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado. Temas no STIP: Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). Instrumentos: Bolsas de estudo, de pesquisa e de pós-graduação; orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: In accordance with the National Development Plan 2019-2024, affirmative actions are implemented to provide support focused on historically excluded population groups. Between 1 September 2020 and 30 June 2021, a total of 3,571 scholarships were administered to support specific populations to promote social inclusion, of which 22.7% (812) went to students from indigenous populations to pursue postgraduate studies, 77.1% (2,754) to Mexican mothers who are heads of household to pursue full-time, school-based professional studies, and 0.2% (5) to incorporate students with disabilities to pursue postgraduate studies. (continuação) Of these, 19.9% had motor disabilities, 64.5% had sensory disabilities (hearing, visual, language and communication), 9.1% had multiple disabilities and 6.5% had mental disabilities.

nome: Debate de política de CTI 2025: Recursos humanos em CTI na Argentina (OECD STIP Compass)
outrosNomes: STI human resources debates (ARG)
categoria: Debate de Política / OECD STIP Compass
tipo: Debate nacional de política de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)
detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass, Policy Debates 2025 (texto informado pelo governo da Argentina, atualizado em 10/04/2025). Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Argentina. The ongoing debate is centered on the structure and criteria of career paths for researchers and technologists. Recent policy proposals have sought to broaden the scope of technology transfer careers, enhance public-private internships, and revise evaluation criteria to better reflect the diverse contributions of individuals in these fields. In this context, discussions also consider the need to strengthen merit-based selection and progression mechanisms, as well as to prioritise strategic areas aligned with national development goals. These initiatives are essential as they aim to create more dynamic career pathways in science, technology, and innovation. By updating the evaluation criteria, we can ensure that a wider array of contributions are recognised, including activities related to innovation, technology development, collaboration with industry, and the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, thereby fostering a more diverse and innovative research environment. Additionally, promoting public-private internships can bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, enhancing the skill sets of researchers and technologists, and contribute to improving the employability and mobility of highly skilled human resources across sectors. The expansion of technology transfer careers is also a significant step. It opens up opportunities for professionals to engage directly with the market and society, applying their expertise to real-world challenges and enhancing the impact of scientific research on societal advancement. At the same time, there is an ongoing discussion on how to optimize the allocation of public resources for human capital development, including a shift towards more targeted and impactful funding schemes that prioritise excellence and critical mass over fragmentation. This is complemented by efforts to strengthen linkages between academia, public research organisations, and the productive sector, as well as to promote more flexible career trajectories, including temporary mobility between public and private institutions.

detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass, Policy Debates 2025 (texto informado pelo governo do Brasil, atualizado em 20/02/2025). Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Brasil. STEM Focus: There is a pressing need to enhance both the quantity and quality of STEM graduates in Brazil, as these disciplines are crucial to the country's main research and innovation opportunities. Initiatives are underway to improve science education in schools and to stimulate interest in scientific careers among secondary and undergraduate students. National Interests and Opportunities: This debate focuses on how Brazil's principal research and innovation interests and opportunities should guide the allocation of public resources and the establishment of evaluative incentives. These incentives are designed to foster human resources for research and innovation. The possibility of integrating mission-oriented innovation policy principles within the Brazilian STI policy framework is currently being examined.

In alignment with the new development model promoted by the Chilean Government, which focuses on productive diversification, socio-ecological sustainability, and effective decentralization of growth, there is a consolidated effort to strengthen public investment in Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation (STKI). This effort is recognised as a strategic pillar for the country's productive transformation. The recent establishment of the Productivity and Development Fund, financed through revenues from lithium exploitation, marks a significant step towards creating a higher economic value with territorial justice. However, structural challenges remain, particularly the need for a sustained increase in the gross domestic expenditure on research and development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP (0.39% to the year 2022). This persistent gap limits Chile's capacity to address ongoing global transitions. The Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation (MinCiencia) acknowledges the development of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and biotechnologies. These technologies not only offer an opportunity to enhance national productivity but are also crucial in tackling significant challenges like the climate emergency, disaster resilience, and improving the quality of life. Addressing these issues requires a policy approach that integrates technological infrastructure, enabling regulatory frameworks, and the training of human capital, focusing on rights, equity, and territorial relevance. The Government's strategy centers on mission-driven STKI as a core element of public action, aimed at an economic model that protects ecosystems, reduces structural, gender and territorial inequalities, and builds technological sovereignty.

It recognises knowledge not as a luxury, but as an essential tool to build a more just, inclusive, and sustainable future for Chile. In addition to the national STI policy, Chile is developing other strategic policies. These include the artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the CTCI gender policy, the green hydrogen strategy, and a roadmap for transitioning to a circular economy. Furthermore, the Better Work in Research Agenda is an initiative that seeks to monitor research careers or trajectories and the conditions surrounding them, complementing the efforts to fund research infrastructure adequately. Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Chile. In Chile, current policy debates on government support for human resources for research and innovation (R&D&I) are increasingly focusing on the need to transition from a model centred almost exclusively on academic training to a more comprehensive approach. This new model aims to promote effective insertion, intersectoral mobility, and the development of career paths within the science, technology, knowledge, and innovation (STKI) system. One of the primary concerns is the limited articulation between the growing volume of advanced human capital, which is mainly formed through national and international scholarships, and the actual employment opportunities available in the public, private, and productive sectors. This mismatch has drawn criticism from academic communities as well as researcher unions and associations, which are advocating for a review of the sustainability of the current system. A second focal point of the debate centers on the need to redefine the instruments that support labour market insertion, particularly in the private sector and intermediate institutions such as technology centres, NGOs, and regional governments. These areas face structural barriers including low demand for R&D, a lack of differentiated tax incentives, and a weak regional institutional framework for absorbing scientific-technological talent. In response, proposals are being put forward that suggest more flexible insertion programmes, new training schemes oriented towards innovation and entrepreneurship, and enhanced capacity building in R&D management and technology transfer. Furthermore, there is active discussion on the need to revise the criteria for evaluating academic and scientific performance. The proposed revisions include incorporating dimensions such as engagement with the environment, participation in social innovation, and intersectoral collaboration. These debates indicate a paradigm shift towards a more inclusive and flexible human resources policy in ICTC, which is oriented towards maximising the economic and social impact of knowledge.

The ongoing debates in the governance of science, technology, and innovation (STI) policies are centred on ensuring that strategic direction is aligned with public interest, social justice, and territorial action. There is a growing consensus on the need to transition away from centralized and technocratic models towards frameworks that promote representative and equal participation, free from conflicts of interest. Furthermore, there is a call for the inclusion of differential, gender, and territorial approaches in policy-making. This is crucial for addressing the diverse needs and challenges across different regions and communities. The coordination between national and local levels, exemplified by initiatives such as the Departmental Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (CODECTI, which serves as the space for coordination and consultation of STI policy in each department of the country), is essential for effective governance. Additionally, there is a push to broaden the social base of the national system of science, technology and innovation (SNCTeI) by acknowledging the contributions of non-academic actors and embracing diverse forms of knowledge. These discussions highlight the importance of evolving governance models to be more inclusive and representative of a wider array of stakeholders and perspectives.

The main debates currently revolve around sustainable financing, effective regulation, and the need for a territorial approach that connects the five development helices: the State, academia, the business sector, civil society, and the environment. In Colombia and the region, the private sector benefits significantly from subsidies without adequately investing in strategic areas such as technology. In response to this situation, the Mission-Oriented Public Policy (PIIOM) has been adopted, through which the State directs public financing toward achieving strategic objectives such as clean energy and the bioeconomy. At the same time, there is an ongoing discussion about bureaucratic barriers and the accessibility of government programs and resources that aim to foster business innovation and entrepreneurship. Many entrepreneurs highlight the difficulties they face in accessing incentives, the lack of coordination among public entities, and the need to simplify administrative procedures. They also call for ensuring a more agile and effective implementation of programs and projects that stimulate innovation. Access to financing is one of the most debated topics, focusing on the effectiveness of state financial instruments and the urgent need to create mechanisms to provide seed capital. Another important area of debate concerns the need for differentiated public policies to reduce gender gaps, foster female and minority entrepreneurship, and strengthen the popular economy. Additionally, concerns are raised about the effectiveness of coordination among national systems related to science, technology, innovation, education, foreign trade, and even international cooperation. Persistent criticism points to fragmentation, the lack of a long-term vision, weak inter-institutional coordination, and the limited impact of dispersed policies—all of which hinder sustained progress in innovation.

Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Costa Rica. In Costa Rica, policy discussions on human resources for research and innovation are increasingly focused on strengthening the national talent pipeline, particularly in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. While the number of researchers per capita and PhD graduates in priority areas faced challenges (398 per million inhabitants), stakeholders across academia, government, and industry are actively promoting initiatives to expand advanced training programs, foster international mobility, and align educational pathways with emerging technological demands. Current efforts aim to improve incentives for talent retention, support reintegration of researchers trained abroad, and encourage interdisciplinary and applied research careers. These actions are being framed within broader strategies such as the National STI Policy and the National AI Strategy, reflecting a shared commitment to developing a robust and future-ready research and innovation workforce. Another key focus of current policy discussions is strengthening the integration of researchers into the private sector and expanding stable, long-term career pathways in public research institutions. Stakeholders are advancing proposals for public-private research fellowships, as well as reforms in recruitment and career progression mechanisms to foster interdisciplinary and applied research. In parallel, efforts are underway to align postgraduate scholarship programs with strategic national priorities—including artificial intelligence, bioeconomy, and clean technologies—ensuring that talent development responds to the evolving demands of the innovation ecosystem. There is also growing momentum to promote innovation-oriented skills among students and professionals through short-term training, mentorships, and stronger academia-industry collaboration, building a more agile and responsive STI workforce. Although some of these ideas are incorporated in recent strategies like the PNCTI and the National AI Strategy, significant policy shifts are still necessary.

Trecho sobre mulheres ou gênero: "Its goals include strengthening Mexico's capabilities and reducing its technological dependence by training and consolidating the scientific, technological, humanities, and research community with a focus on gender parity.". On November 28, 2024, the Organic Law of the Federal Public Administration was amended, creating the Secretariat of Science, Humanities, Technology, and Innovation, which is set to commence operations on January 1, 2025. The primary objective of the Secretariat is to ensure that every individual has the right to enjoy the benefits of scientific development, humanistic progress, and technological innovation. The new policy framework in Mexico aims to transform the nation into a sovereign scientific and technological power. This transformation is envisioned through the promotion of collaborative research, technological development, and innovation in strategic sectors, ultimately fostering development that leads to shared well-being and prosperity. Currently, the integration of the Science, Humanities, Technology, and Innovation Sectoral Programme is in progress. Its goals include strengthening Mexico's capabilities and reducing its technological dependence by training and consolidating the scientific, technological, humanities, and research community with a focus on gender parity. The programme also promotes technological development by maturing and scaling technologies that align with regional and national priorities, thereby contributing to social well-being. It aims to generate knowledge through basic and interdisciplinary research and to strengthen the infrastructure necessary to tackle priority issues. Additionally, it seeks to implement mechanisms for linkage, modernisation, and technology transfer and innovation between the academic, productive, public, and social sectors. These efforts are aligned with national priorities and are oriented towards social well-being through inter-institutional collaboration networks that carry out strategic projects, promote the transfer of knowledge and innovation, and address local, national, and international challenges. The transition from the National Council for Humanities, Sciences, and Technologies to a Secretariat involved the regulatory harmonisation of many activities governing the sector.

Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: México. Mexico has recently undergone significant changes, and the scientific sector is no exception. The reform of Article 3 of the Constitution in 2019 led to the creation of the new Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies, and Innovation. This law recognises that every individual has the right to enjoy the benefits of scientific and technological innovation and mandates the State to provide sufficient resources and incentives. It also guarantees free access to public postgraduate programmes recognised within the National Postgraduate System. The political debate surrounding government support for human resources in research and innovation acknowledges the budgetary constraints that must be addressed to ensure this constitutional right for everyone, irrespective of their socioeconomic or cultural conditions. There are two major debates in this area. The first concerns the training of the scientific and humanities community, specifically whether funding private higher education institutions and research centres imposes a budgetary burden that distorts plural and equitable access to science at the expense of collective benefit. A similar discussion arises around the equitable distribution for postgraduate studies abroad versus prioritising support within the national system. The second debate focuses on strengthening the scientific community, including the prioritisation of support for researchers in the public sector versus those in the private or foreign sectors. This debate extends to how the community sustains itself, questioning whether support mechanisms should prioritise productivity or career development, while respecting diversity of thought and socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds. Additionally, there is a discussion on whether scientific activity should address public problems. Given the existing disparities across different regions of the country, the scientific community experiences inequalities that prompt a broader dialogue on these issues.

Peru has made significant strides in enhancing the capacities, skills, and competencies of its human capital in the fields of science, technology, and innovation. The country is actively promoting doctoral programs through inter-institutional alliances and increasing funding for scholarships and internships. Currently, internships are in both academia and industry, with a higher proportion in academia because in Peru, unfortunately, we have not made progress in implementing incentives for the incorporation of researchers in technology companies. Additionally, incentives are being provided to improve the retention and attraction of talent, thereby increasing dedication to STI activities. Training for technological managers in science, technology, and innovation is also being emphasized as part of these policy initiatives. Furthermore, Peru is committed to promoting the continued participation of women, girls, and adolescents in scientific research, technological development, and innovation activities. This is being achieved through strategic alliances with educational institutions, research centers, and international organizations that support gender equity in the scientific and technological fields. These efforts are part of a broader strategy to build a robust framework for research and innovation, ensuring that Peru remains competitive and innovative in the global STI landscape.

Sim — Are there shelters for women affected by violence: sim (Shelter Houses; Shelter Services for Women Victims of Violence); Are there health services for women affected by violence: sim (Women's Hospitals); Are there psychological services for women affected by violence: sim (Healthcare for People in Situations of Sexual Violence; Women's Hospitals; Women's Reference Centers/Women's…); Are there livelihood support services for women affected by violence: sim (Rent Allowance for Women Victims of Domestic Violence; Houses of Brazilian Women Services to Promote…). 1.4 Há um mecanismo institucional para monitorar leis, planos e programas sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim (fonte: Ministério das Mulheres). Sim (base legal: Civil Code, Art. 1642). 3.2 A lei proíbe discriminação na contratação por estado civil, situação parental ou idade? Sim — Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on marital status: sim (Law No. 9.029/1995, Art. 1; Constitution of the Federal Republic of Brazil, Art. 7(XXX)); Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on parental status: sim (Law No. 9.029/1995, Art. 1; Consolidated Labor Laws, Art. 373A(I)); Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on age: sim (Law No. 9.029/1995, Art. 1; Consolidated Labor Laws, Art. 373A(I)). 3.3 A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (base legal: Law No. 9.029/1995, Art. 1; Consolidated Labor Laws, Art. 373A(II)). 3.4 A lei permite que trabalhadores peçam trabalho flexível? Sim — Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the time of work: sim (Law No. 14457/2022, Art. 8(v) and 14); Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the place of work: sim (Consolidated Labor Laws, Arts. 75-A to F). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 3.1 Há um órgão especializado que recebe denúncias de discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (fonte: Gender and Race Equity Program 7th Edition). 3.3 O governo oferece materiais para o setor privado adotar trabalho flexível? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.4 Algum plano ou estratégia nacional trata do acesso das mulheres ao mercado de trabalho? Sim — Does the plan or strategy include measures to increase women’s access to the labor market: sim (National Plan for Equal Pay and Employment between Women and Men); Does the plan or strategy include institutional arrangements to monitor the implementation of the plan or strategy: sim (National Plan for Equal Pay and Employment between Women and Men); Does the plan or strategy provide for result targets and indicators: sim (National Plan for Equal Pay and Employment between Women and Men).

Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 7.1 A lei estabelece a oferta de creches (cuidado infantil em centros)? Sim — Does the law establish the provision of center-based childcare services by the government: sim (Law No. 9.394 of 1996, Arts. 4, 10, 19, 29 and 30(I); Federal Constitution of Brazil, Art. 208(IV); Law No.…); Does the law establish the provision of childcare services by private centers: sim (Law No. 9.394 of 1996, Arts. 18(II), 19(II), 29 and 30(I)); Does the law establish the provision of childcare services by employers not conditional on female employees: não (Labor Law of 1 May 1943, Art. 389; Ordinance MTP No. 671 of 8 November 2021, Art. 121; Law 14457 of 21…). 7.2 A lei estabelece alguma forma de apoio às famílias para o custo da creche? Sim — Is the legal age of marriage 18 or higher for boys and girls: sim (Ley de Matrimonio Civil No. 19.947, Arts. 2, 4 y 5(3)); Is the law free of parental consent exceptions to the legal age of marriage (or is the age of marriage with parental…: sim; Is marriage under the legal age void or voidable: sim (Ley de Matrimonio Civil No. 19.947, Art. 2); Are there penalties for adults who authorize, celebrate, register, or enter into child marriage: sim (Código Penal, Art. 388). 1.2 A lei trata do assédio sexual? Em parte (0,25 de 1) — Is there legislation on sexual harassment in employment with criminal penalties or civil remedies: não; Is there legislation on sexual harassment in education/schools with criminal penalties or civil remedies: não; Is there legislation on sexual harassment in public places (or on transportation) with criminal penalties or civil…: sim (Código Penal, Art. 494 ter); Is there legislation on cyberharassment or cyberstalking with criminal penalties or civil remedies: não. 1.3 A lei trata da violência doméstica? Não — Is there a law or legal provision on domestic violence: sim (Ley No. 20.066; Ley 21.675); Does legislation on domestic violence establish criminal penalties: não; Does legislation on domestic violence provide for protection orders: sim (Ley 21.675 (Ley No. 20.066 de Violencia Intrafamiliar, Arts. 7 y 9)); Does legislation on domestic violence address physical, psychological, financial/economic, and sexual violence…: sim; Does legislation on domestic violence address physical violence: sim (Ley No. 20.066 de Violencia Intrafamiliar, Art. 5); Does legislation on domestic violence address psychological violence: sim (Ley No. 20.066 de Violencia Intrafamiliar, Art. 5); Does legislation on domestic violence address economic or financial violence: sim (Ley 21.675, Arts. 6(4) and 54(5) (Ley 20066, Art. 5)); Does legislation on domestic violence address sexual violence, including marital rape: sim (Ley 21.675, Art. 54(5) (Ley 20066, Art. 5); Código Penal, Arts. 361 y 369).

Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 56,25; marco de apoio 79,25; percepção da aplicação 46,88. Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 1.1 Há um plano de ação ou estratégia sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim — Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for prevention measures: sim (Plan Nacional por el Derecho a Vidas Libres de Violencia de Género para Mujeres, Niñas y Diversidades, Línea…); Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women indicate the institutions responsible for its implementation: sim (Plan Nacional por el Derecho a Vidas Libres de Violencia de Género para Mujeres, Niñas y Diversidades, III.…); Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for result targets and indicators: sim (Plan Nacional por el Derecho a Vidas Libres de Violencia de Género para Mujeres, Niñas y Diversidades, 2.3). 1.2 Há mecanismos que facilitam o acesso à justiça em casos de violência contra a mulher? Em parte (0,67 de 1) — Are there special police or prosecutorial units on violence against women: sim (Unidad de Género de la Fiscalía Nacional del Ministerio Público); Are there special courts or procedures for cases of violence against women: não; Is legal aid provided for cases of violence against women: sim (Centros de las Mujeres[+]; Centros de Atención Especializada en Violencias de Género). 1.3 O governo oferece ou financia serviços para mulheres afetadas pela violência? Em parte (0,5 de 1) — Are there shelters for women affected by violence: sim (Residencias Transitorias, Ministerio de la Mujer y la Equidad de Género); Are there health services for women affected by violence: não; Are there psychological services for women affected by violence: sim (Centros de las Mujeres[+]; Centros de Atención Especializada en Violencias de Género); Are there livelihood support services for women affected by violence: não. 1.4 Há um mecanismo institucional para monitorar leis, planos e programas sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim (fonte: Ministerio de la Mujer y la Equidad de Género). Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 1.1 A lei trata do casamento infantil: 4 de 4; 1.2 A lei trata do assédio sexual: 0,5 de 4; 1.3 A lei trata da violência doméstica: 0 de 4; 1.4 A lei trata do feminicídio: 3 de 4. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens). "Não se aplica": falta a lei ou o mecanismo que a pergunta pressupõe.

Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 3.1 A lei permite que a mulher consiga um emprego da mesma forma que o homem? Sim (base legal: Código Civil, Art. 150). 3.2 A lei proíbe discriminação na contratação por estado civil, situação parental ou idade? Sim — Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on marital status: sim (Código del Trabajo, Art. 2); Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on parental status: sim (Código del Trabajo, Art. 2); Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on age: sim (Código del Trabajo, Art. 2). 3.3 A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Art. 2). 3.4 A lei permite que trabalhadores peçam trabalho flexível? Sim — Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the time of work: sim (Ley 21.561, Art. 1.2); Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the place of work: sim (Código del Trabajo, Art. 152 quáter G and O). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 3.1 Há um órgão especializado que recebe denúncias de discriminação de gênero no emprego? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.2 O governo promove ações de conscientização sobre recrutamento sem discriminação de gênero? Sim (fonte: Programa Buenas Prácticas Laborales con Equidad de Género). 3.3 O governo oferece materiais para o setor privado adotar trabalho flexível? Sim (fonte: Dirección del Trabajo de Chile- Consultas). 3.4 Algum plano ou estratégia nacional trata do acesso das mulheres ao mercado de trabalho? Sim — Does the plan or strategy include measures to increase women’s access to the labor market: sim (Plan Nacional de Equidad Laboral 2021-2030); Does the plan or strategy include institutional arrangements to monitor the implementation of the plan or strategy: sim (Plan Nacional de Equidad Laboral 2021-2030); Does the plan or strategy provide for result targets and indicators: sim (Plan Nacional de Equidad Laboral 2021-2030).

Não (nenhuma disposição legal aplicável localizada pelo WBL). 4.2 A mulher pode trabalhar à noite da mesma forma que o homem? Sim (nenhuma restrição legal localizada pelo WBL). 4.3 A mulher pode trabalhar em atividades consideradas perigosas da mesma forma que o homem? Sim — Can a woman work in a job deemed hazardous: sim; Can a woman work in a job deemed arduous: sim; Can a woman work in a job deemed morally inappropriate: sim; Is the law free of legal provisions that explicitly give the relevant government authority the power to restrict or…: sim. 4.4 A mulher pode trabalhar nos diferentes setores da economia da mesma forma que o homem? Sim — Can a woman work in the mining sector: sim; Can a woman work in the construction sector: sim; Can a woman work in the manufacturing sector: sim; Can a woman work in the agriculture sector: sim; Can a woman work in the transportation sector: sim; Can a woman work in the energy sector: sim; Can a woman work in the water sector: sim; Is the law free of legal provisions that explicitly give the relevant government authority the power to restrict or…: sim. Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 87,5; marco de apoio 75; percepção da aplicação 78,13. Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 6.1 Há licença remunerada para as mães? Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Arts. 195, 197 bis and 198) — duração da licença das mães: 210 dias. 6.2 Os benefícios da licença das mães são pagos pelo governo? Sim (base legal: Decreto Ley No. 150, Arts. 2 y 4; Decreto Ley No. 44 of 1978, Art. 8) — quem paga o benefício: governo. 6.3 Há licença remunerada para os pais? Em parte (0,5 de 1) (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Art. 195) — duração da licença dos pais: 7 dias. 6.4 A demissão de trabalhadoras grávidas é proibida? Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Arts. 174, 194 y 201). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 6.1 É possível pedir o benefício de maternidade por um único processo do governo? Sim (fonte: Superintendencia de Seguridad Social; Código del Trabajo, Art. 197). 6.2 Há incentivos para que os pais tirem a licença-paternidade no nascimento de um filho? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 6.3 O governo publica dados anônimos por sexo sobre o trabalho de cuidado não remunerado? Sim (fonte: Encuesta del Uso del Tiempo). 6.4 Há iniciativas do governo para promover a divisão igual do trabalho doméstico e de cuidado entre homens e mulheres? Sim (fonte: Política Nacional de Apoyos y Cuidados). Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 6.1 Há licença remunerada para as mães: 4 de 4; 6.2 Os benefícios da licença das mães são pagos pelo governo: 3 de 4; 6.3 Há licença remunerada para os pais: 1,5 de 4; 6.4 A demissão de trabalhadoras grávidas é proibida: 4 de 4. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens).

Respostas: Há licença remunerada para as mães: sim; Os benefícios da licença das mães são pagos pelo governo: sim; Há licença remunerada para os pais: em parte (0,5 de 1); A demissão de trabalhadoras grávidas é proibida: sim; É possível pedir o benefício de maternidade por um único processo do governo: sim; Há incentivos para que os pais tirem a licença-paternidade no nascimento de um filho: não; O governo publica dados anônimos por sexo sobre o trabalho de cuidado não remunerado: sim; Há iniciativas do governo para promover a divisão igual do trabalho doméstico e de cuidado entre homens e mulheres: sim. detalhes: Fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law (WBL) 2026, base de dados de 23/02/2026 (metodologia WBL 2.0). Tema: Cuidado infantil (creches) (Childcare). País: Chile. Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 100; marco de apoio 75; percepção da aplicação 50. Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 7.1 A lei estabelece a oferta de creches (cuidado infantil em centros)? Sim — Does the law establish the provision of center-based childcare services by the government: sim (Decreto con Fuerza de Ley No. 2 de 2009, Arts. 3(a)(b) y 4; Ley No. 17301 de 1970, Arts. 1-3; Decreto 1574…); Does the law establish the provision of childcare services by private centers: sim (Ley No. 20832 de 2015, Art. 3; Decreto con Fuerza de Ley No. 2 de 2009, Arts. 4 y 18; Decreto No. 1574 de…); Does the law establish the provision of childcare services by employers not conditional on female employees: não (Código del Trabajo de 2002, Art. 203). 7.2 A lei estabelece alguma forma de apoio às famílias para o custo da creche? Sim — Does the law establish any form of financial support for families for childcare services: sim (Decreto No. 1574 de 1971, Art. 38; Sitio Web Oficial de Chile Atiende, Junta Nacional de Jardines Infantiles); Does the law establish tax incentives for families for childcare services: sim (Decreto Ley No. 824, Art. 55-Ter). 7.3 A lei estabelece alguma forma de apoio a creches não estatais (privadas ou de empregadores)? Sim — Does the law establish any form of financial support for private childcare centers: sim (Decreto No. 67 de 2010, Arts. 10, 14, 16-17; Decreto con Fuerza de Ley No. 2 de 2009, Art. 3(b); Sitio Web…); Does the law establish tax incentives for private childcare centers: não; Does the law establish any form of financial support for employers for providing or supporting childcare services for…: não; Does the law establish tax incentives for employers for providing or supporting childcare services for their employees: não. 7.4 A lei estabelece padrões de qualidade para as creches? Sim — Does the law establish caregiver-to-child ratio or a maximum group size in childcare centers (public or private): sim (Decreto No. 315 de 2010, Arts. 5 y 10; Decreto No. 1574 de 1971, Art. 47(2)(B)); Does the law establish a minimum level of specialized education or training for educators in childcare centers (public…: sim (Decreto No. 315 de 2010, Arts. 11(b)(c); Decreto con Fuerza de Ley No. 2 de 2009, Art. 46(g); Decreto No.…);
fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law 2026 (tema Childcare); World Bank. 2026. "Women, Business and the Law" [dataset]. Washington, DC: World Bank. https://wbl.worldbank.org/en/wbl-data

(continuação) Does the law establish mandatory periodic inspection of childcare centers (public or private) by authorized bodies or…: sim (Ley No. 20832 de 2015, Art. 8; Ley No. 20529 de 2011, Art. 53). Sim (fonte: Sitio Web Oficial de Chile Atiende, Jardines infantiles y Salas Cunas de JUNJI). 7.3 Há um procedimento claro para prestadores não estatais pedirem apoio financeiro do governo? Sim — Is There a Clearly Outlined Application Procedure to Request Financial Support from the Government for Childcare…: sim (Manual del Programa Transferencia de Fondos, pgs. 6-8); Is There a Clearly Outlined Application Procedure to Request Financial Support from the Government for Childcare…: não. 7.4 O governo publica relatórios sobre a qualidade das creches? Não — Does the government publish reports of a broad nature benchmarking the quality of childcare services: não; Does the government provide an open-data information system or publish reports that assess individual childcare…: não se aplica. Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 7.1 A lei estabelece a oferta de creches (cuidado infantil em centros): 3 de 4; 7.2 A lei estabelece alguma forma de apoio às famílias para o custo da creche: 2 de 4; 7.3 A lei estabelece alguma forma de apoio a creches não estatais (privadas ou de empregadores): 2 de 4; 7.4 A lei estabelece padrões de qualidade para as creches: 1 de 4. "Não se aplica": falta a lei ou o mecanismo que a pergunta pressupõe.
fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law 2026 (tema Childcare); World Bank. 2026. "Women, Business and the Law" [dataset]. Washington, DC: World Bank. https://wbl.worldbank.org/en/wbl-data

Sim — Does the government publish sex-disaggregated data on women-owned or women-led businesses: sim (Registro de Empresas y Sociedades); Does the government publish sex-disaggregated data on women in private sector leadership positions: sim (REPORTE DE INDICADORES DE GÉNERO EN LAS EMPRESAS EN CHILE, Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Economy and…). 8.3 Há programas do governo de capacitação ou desenvolvimento de negócios para empreendedoras? Sim (fonte: Programa Mujer Emprende; Escuela Mujer Emprende). 8.4 Há serviços do governo para ampliar o acesso de mulheres e empreendedoras a serviços financeiros? Sim — Is there a national financial inclusion strategy or a national strategy with a dedicated section focusing on women’s…: sim (Estrategia Nacional de Inclusión Financiera); Does the government provide programs on access to financial services or resources to women or female entrepreneurs: sim (Garantía Fogain Mujer - Chile Emprende, Ministry of Economy; Capital Abeja Emprende, Ministry of Economy…). detalhes: Fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law (WBL) 2026, base de dados de 23/02/2026 (metodologia WBL 2.0). Tema: Aposentadoria (Pension). País: Chile. Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 79,25; marco de apoio 100; percepção da aplicação 48,75. Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 10.1 As idades de aposentadoria de mulheres e homens são iguais? Em parte (0,5 de 1) — Are the Ages at Which a Woman and a Man Can Retire with Full Pension Benefits the Same: 0 (Decreto Ley No. 3500, Art. 3); idade dos homens (benefício integral): 65 anos; idade das mulheres (benefício integral): 60 anos; Are the Ages at Which a Woman and a Man Can Retire with Partial Pension Benefits the Same: 1; idade dos homens (benefício parcial): não se aplica; idade das mulheres (benefício parcial): não se aplica. 10.2 A idade de aposentadoria compulsória é igual para mulheres e homens? Sim (nenhuma disposição legal aplicável localizada pelo WBL) — idade compulsória das mulheres: não se aplica; idade compulsória dos homens: não se aplica. 10.3 Os períodos de afastamento para cuidar dos filhos contam no cálculo da aposentadoria? Sim (base legal: Ley No. 20.255, Arts. 74-76). 10.4 A lei garante benefícios iguais de pensão por morte para os cônjuges? Em parte (0,67 de 1) — Does the law specify equal eligibility criteria for widows and widowers to access survivor pension benefits: sim (Decreto Ley No. 3500, Art. 6); Does the law specify an equal minimum age at which spouses can receive survivor benefits: não; Does the law specify that benefit payments are paid in installments for widows and widowers: sim (Decreto Ley No. 3500, Article 62). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 10.1 Há incentivos para aumentar a aposentadoria das mulheres? Sim (fonte: Compendio de Normas del Sistema de Pensiones, Título VI). 10.2 Há um procedimento para contestar as decisões sobre o benefício de aposentadoria? Sim (fonte: Codigo del Trabajo, Art. 420). 10.3 Há ações de conscientização sobre o acesso à informação sobre aposentadoria? Sim (fonte: Chile Atiende; Superintendencia de Pensiones). 10.4 O governo publica dados anônimos por sexo sobre a idade real de aposentadoria e o valor dos benefícios? Sim — Does the government publish sex-disaggregated data on actual retirement ages: sim (Estadísticas Superintendencia de Pensiones); Does the government publish sex-disaggregated data on the actual amount of received pension benefits: sim (Estadísticas Superintendencia de Pensiones).
fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law 2026 (tema Pension); World Bank. 2026. "Women, Business and the Law" [dataset]. Washington, DC: World Bank. https://wbl.worldbank.org/en/wbl-data

detalhes: Fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law, série na metodologia WBL 1.0: painel 1971–2024 (arquivo de 04/03/2024) e WBL 2026 recalculado na metodologia 1.0 (arquivo de 23/02/2026). Evolução das leis sobre os direitos econômicos das mulheres no Chile. País: Chile. Índice WBL 1.0 (0 a 100; 100 = igualdade plena nas leis): último dado 80 (2026) [série: 2013: 77,5; 2014: 77,5; 2015: 77,5; 2016: 77,5; 2017: 77,5; 2018: 77,5; 2019: 77,5; 2020: 77,5; 2021: 80; 2022: 80; 2023: 80; 2024: 80; 2026: 80]. Pontuação por tema, 2013 → 2026: Mobilidade 100 → 100; Trabalho 75 → 75; Remuneração 75 → 75; Casamento 60 → 80; Parentalidade 100 → 100; Empreendedorismo 75 → 75; Bens 60 → 60; Aposentadoria 75 → 75. Licenças: licença-maternidade remunerada 126 dias em 2013 e 126 dias em 2026; licença-paternidade remunerada 7 dias em 2013 e 7 dias em 2026. Mudanças nas respostas desde 2013: 2021: "A mulher tem os mesmos direitos de se casar de novo que o homem" passou de não para sim (base legal: Ley Núm.21264 modifica Código Civil, Art. 1). Atenção: não há dado 1.0 para 2025; o índice 1.0 tem 8 temas e 35 perguntas e não é comparável com os índices WBL 2.0 de 2026. A planilha de 2026 diz que os dados são de 1º de outubro de 2026, mas foi publicada em fevereiro de 2026; a API do Banco Mundial registra os mesmos dados da edição 2026 como ano 2025.
fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law, painel 1971–2024 e WBL 2026 (1.0); World Bank. 2026. "Women, Business and the Law" [dataset]. Washington, DC: World Bank. https://wbl.worldbank.org/en/wbl-data

detalhes: Fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law (WBL) 2026, base de dados de 23/02/2026 (metodologia WBL 2.0). Tema: Parentalidade: licenças e proteção da gestante (Parenthood). País: Colômbia. Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 100; marco de apoio 75; percepção da aplicação 93,75. Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 6.1 Há licença remunerada para as mães? Sim (base legal: Ley No. 1822 de 2017, Art. 1; Código Sustantivo del Trabajo, Art. 236; Ley No. 2114 de 2021, Art. 2) — duração da licença das mães: 126 dias. 6.2 Os benefícios da licença das mães são pagos pelo governo? Sim (base legal: Decreto 47/2000, Art. 3(2); Ley No. 100/1993, Art. 207) — quem paga o benefício: governo. 6.3 Há licença remunerada para os pais? Sim (base legal: Ley No. 2114 de 2021, Art. 2 para. 2) — duração da licença dos pais: 14 dias. 6.4 A demissão de trabalhadoras grávidas é proibida? Sim (base legal: Código Sustantivo del Trabajo, Art. 239). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 6.1 É possível pedir o benefício de maternidade por um único processo do governo? Sim (fonte: Ley No. 100/1993, Art. 207). 6.2 Há incentivos para que os pais tirem a licença-paternidade no nascimento de um filho? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 6.3 O governo publica dados anônimos por sexo sobre o trabalho de cuidado não remunerado? Sim (fonte: Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística, Cuenta Satélite de Economía del Cuidado (CSEC)). 6.4 Há iniciativas do governo para promover a divisão igual do trabalho doméstico e de cuidado entre homens e mulheres? Sim (fonte: Política Nacional de Cuidado, CONPES 4143). Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 6.1 Há licença remunerada para as mães: 4 de 4; 6.2 Os benefícios da licença das mães são pagos pelo governo: 3 de 4; 6.3 Há licença remunerada para os pais: 4 de 4; 6.4 A demissão de trabalhadoras grávidas é proibida: 4 de 4. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens).

Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 6.3 O governo publica dados anônimos por sexo sobre o trabalho de cuidado não remunerado? Sim (fonte: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos, Encuesta Nacional de Uso del Tiempo 2022). 6.4 Há iniciativas do governo para promover a divisão igual do trabalho doméstico e de cuidado entre homens e mulheres? Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 1.1 Há um plano de ação ou estratégia sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim — Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for prevention measures: sim (Plan Nacional para Prevenir y Erradicar la Violencia Contra las Mujeres); Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women indicate the institutions responsible for its implementation: sim (Plan Nacional para Prevenir y Erradicar la Violencia Contra las Mujeres, Cap. 10); Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for result targets and indicators: sim (Plan Nacional para Prevenir y Erradicar la Violencia Contra las Mujeres, Indicadores para seguimiento y…). 1.2 Há mecanismos que facilitam o acesso à justiça em casos de violência contra a mulher? Sim — Are there special police or prosecutorial units on violence against women: sim (Unidades Especializadas de Violencia de Género, Fiscalía General del Estado; DINAF, Policía Nacional); Are there special courts or procedures for cases of violence against women: sim (Unidades Judiciales Especializadas contra la Violencia a la Mujer); Is legal aid provided for cases of violence against women: sim (Centro de Equidad y Justicia; Defensoria Pública). 1.3 O governo oferece ou financia serviços para mulheres afetadas pela violência? Em parte (0,75 de 1) — Are there shelters for women affected by violence: sim (Casa de la Mujer); Are there health services for women affected by violence: sim (Salas de Primera Acogida); Are there psychological services for women affected by violence: sim (Salas de Primera Acogida; Centros de Equidad y Justicia); Are there livelihood support services for women affected by violence: não. 1.4 Há um mecanismo institucional para monitorar leis, planos e programas sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim (fonte: Consejo Nacional para la Igualdad de Género). Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 1.1 A lei trata do casamento infantil: 0 de 4; 1.2 A lei trata do assédio sexual: 1,13 de 4; 1.3 A lei trata da violência doméstica: 3 de 4; 1.4 A lei trata do feminicídio: 2 de 4. "Não se aplica": falta a lei ou o mecanismo que a pergunta pressupõe.

Índice WBL 1.0 (0 a 100; 100 = igualdade plena nas leis): último dado 92,5 (2026) [série: 2013: 84,375; 2014: 84,375; 2015: 84,375; 2016: 84,375; 2017: 89,375; 2018: 89,375; 2019: 89,375; 2020: 89,375; 2021: 89,375; 2022: 89,375; 2023: 89,375; 2024: 89,375; 2026: 92,5]. Pontuação por tema, 2013 → 2026: Mobilidade 100 → 100; Trabalho 100 → 100; Remuneração 100 → 100; Casamento 60 → 100; Parentalidade 40 → 40; Empreendedorismo 75 → 100; Bens 100 → 100; Aposentadoria 100 → 100. Licenças: licença-maternidade remunerada 84 dias em 2013 e 84 dias em 2026; licença-paternidade remunerada 14 dias em 2013 e 15 dias em 2026. Mudanças nas respostas desde 2013: 2017: "A mulher pode obter o divórcio da mesma forma que o homem" passou de não para sim (base legal: Ley Reformatoria Código Civil de 2015, Art. 110); 2017: "A mulher tem os mesmos direitos de se casar de novo que o homem" passou de não para sim (base legal: Ley Reformatoria Código Civil de 2015, Art. 106); 2026: "A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no acesso ao crédito" passou de não para sim (reforma legal, segundo o WBL). Atenção: não há dado 1.0 para 2025; o índice 1.0 tem 8 temas e 35 perguntas e não é comparável com os índices WBL 2.0 de 2026. A planilha de 2026 diz que os dados são de 1º de outubro de 2026, mas foi publicada em fevereiro de 2026; a API do Banco Mundial registra os mesmos dados da edição 2026 como ano 2025.

Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 3.1 A lei permite que a mulher consiga um emprego da mesma forma que o homem? Sim (nenhuma restrição legal localizada pelo WBL). 3.2 A lei proíbe discriminação na contratação por estado civil, situação parental ou idade? Não — Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on marital status: não; Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on parental status: não; Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on age: não. 3.3 A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Art. 30(12)). 3.4 A lei permite que trabalhadores peçam trabalho flexível? Em parte (0,5 de 1) — Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the time of work: não; Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the place of work: sim (Ley de Regulación del Teletrabajo, Art. 6). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 3.1 Há um órgão especializado que recebe denúncias de discriminação de gênero no emprego? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.2 O governo promove ações de conscientização sobre recrutamento sem discriminação de gênero? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.3 O governo oferece materiais para o setor privado adotar trabalho flexível? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.4 Algum plano ou estratégia nacional trata do acesso das mulheres ao mercado de trabalho? Não — Does the plan or strategy include measures to increase women’s access to the labor market: não; Does the plan or strategy include institutional arrangements to monitor the implementation of the plan or strategy: não; Does the plan or strategy provide for result targets and indicators: não. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens). Sim — Is there a national financial inclusion strategy or a national strategy with a dedicated section focusing on women’s…: sim (Política Nacional de Inclusión Financiera; Programa Nacional de Financiamiento del Desarrollo (PRONAFIDE)…); Does the government provide programs on access to financial services or resources to women or female entrepreneurs: sim (Política Nacional de Inclusión Financiera; Financiamiento para Mujeres Emprendedoras y Empresarias, Fondo…). detalhes: Fonte: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law (WBL) 2026, base de dados de 23/02/2026 (metodologia WBL 2.0). Visão geral dos direitos econômicos das mulheres no Paraguai. País: Paraguai. Índices WBL 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 80,2; marco de apoio 51,55; percepção da aplicação 53,86. Marco legal nos anos anteriores, na mesma metodologia: 2024: 80,2; 2025: 80,2. Pontuação por tema em 2026 (marco legal / marco de apoio / percepção da aplicação): Segurança: violência contra a mulher e assédio 56,25 / 60,5 / 34,38; Mobilidade 100 / 75 / 87,5; Trabalho 62,5 / 25 / 28,13; Remuneração e acesso a setores 100 / 25 / 56,25; Casamento e divórcio 100 / 50 / 75; Parentalidade: licenças e proteção da gestante 100 / 50 / 68,75; Cuidado infantil (creches) 58,25 / 25 / 13,56; Empreendedorismo 50 / 55 / 40,63; Bens e herança 100 / 75 / 84,38; Aposentadoria 75 / 75 / 50. Pergunta 4.4 do marco de apoio, sobre iniciativas do governo para incentivar mulheres a trabalhar em STEM: não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). A planilha traz o marco legal na metodologia 2.0 também para 2024 e 2025; marco de apoio e percepção da aplicação só para 2026. Estes índices não são comparáveis com o índice WBL 1.0 da série histórica. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens).

Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 1.1 Há um plano de ação ou estratégia sobre violência contra a mulher? Não — Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for prevention measures: não; Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women indicate the institutions responsible for its implementation: não; Does the action plan or strategy on violence against women provide for result targets and indicators: não. 1.2 Há mecanismos que facilitam o acesso à justiça em casos de violência contra a mulher? Em parte (0,67 de 1) — Are there special police or prosecutorial units on violence against women: sim (Unidad Especializada de Violencia Familiar y de Género, Ministerio Público); Are there special courts or procedures for cases of violence against women: não; Is legal aid provided for cases of violence against women: sim (Ciudad Mujer Móvil; Servicio de Atención a la Mujer (SEDAMUR); SOS Mujer 137; Unidad Especializada de la…). 1.3 O governo oferece ou financia serviços para mulheres afetadas pela violência? Em parte (0,75 de 1) — Are there shelters for women affected by violence: sim (Casa para mujeres en situación de violencia "Mercedes Sandoval"); Are there health services for women affected by violence: sim (Hospital de Trauma “Manuel Giagni”; Casa para mujeres en situación de violencia "Mercedes Sandoval"); Are there psychological services for women affected by violence: sim (Centro Ciudad Mujer; Servicio de Atención a la Mujer (SEDAMUR); “SOS MUJER” Línea 137; Casa para mujeres en…); Are there livelihood support services for women affected by violence: não. 1.4 Há um mecanismo institucional para monitorar leis, planos e programas sobre violência contra a mulher? Sim (fonte: Ministerio de la Mujer). Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 1.1 A lei trata do casamento infantil: 0 de 4; 1.2 A lei trata do assédio sexual: 0,5 de 4; 1.3 A lei trata da violência doméstica: 2 de 4; 1.4 A lei trata do feminicídio: 3 de 4. Pontuação do tema em 2026 (0 a 100): marco legal 62,5; marco de apoio 25; percepção da aplicação 28,13. Marco legal (o que a lei diz): 3.1 A lei permite que a mulher consiga um emprego da mesma forma que o homem? Sim (base legal: Ley de Reforma Parcial del Código Civil, Art. 7). 3.2 A lei proíbe discriminação na contratação por estado civil, situação parental ou idade? Não — Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on marital status: não; Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on parental status: não; Does the law prohibit discrimination in recruitment based on age: não. 3.3 A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Art. 9; Constitución de la República de Paraguay, Art. 88). 3.4 A lei permite que trabalhadores peçam trabalho flexível? Em parte (0,5 de 1) — Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the time of work: não; Does the law allow employees to request flexibility regarding the place of work: sim (Ley No. 6738 de Teletrabajo, Art. 8). Marco de apoio (políticas, serviços e dados do governo): 3.1 Há um órgão especializado que recebe denúncias de discriminação de gênero no emprego? Sim (fonte: Ley No. 5777, Art. 12). 3.2 O governo promove ações de conscientização sobre recrutamento sem discriminação de gênero? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.3 O governo oferece materiais para o setor privado adotar trabalho flexível? Não (sem evidência suficiente localizada pelo WBL). 3.4 Algum plano ou estratégia nacional trata do acesso das mulheres ao mercado de trabalho? Não — Does the plan or strategy include measures to increase women’s access to the labor market: não; Does the plan or strategy include institutional arrangements to monitor the implementation of the plan or strategy: não; Does the plan or strategy provide for result targets and indicators: não. Percepção da aplicação (especialistas, de 0 a 4): 3.1 A lei permite que a mulher consiga um emprego da mesma forma que o homem: 3 de 4; 3.2 A lei proíbe discriminação na contratação por estado civil, situação parental ou idade: 0 de 4; 3.3 A lei proíbe discriminação de gênero no emprego: 1 de 4; 3.4 A lei permite que trabalhadores peçam trabalho flexível: 0,5 de 4. Como ler: no marco legal e no marco de apoio, cada pergunta vale de 0 a 1 (1 = sim, a lei ou a política existe; valores entre 0 e 1 = atende em parte); a percepção da aplicação vai de 0 a 4; as pontuações de tema e os índices vão de 0 a 100 (100 = igualdade plena entre mulheres e homens).

Sim (base legal: Código del Trabajo, Art. 229). 4.2 A mulher pode trabalhar à noite da mesma forma que o homem? Sim (nenhuma restrição legal localizada pelo WBL). 4.3 A mulher pode trabalhar em atividades consideradas perigosas da mesma forma que o homem? Sim — Can a woman work in a job deemed hazardous: sim; Can a woman work in a job deemed arduous: sim; Can a woman work in a job deemed morally inappropriate: sim; Is the law free of legal provisions that explicitly give the relevant government authority the power to restrict or…: sim. 4.4 A mulher pode trabalhar nos diferentes setores da economia da mesma forma que o homem?
